papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.
RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Efficacy of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Preventing Poststroke Spasticity: A Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke spasticity significantly impairs recovery, yet preventive strategies remain limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in reducing the development and severity of spasticity in patients with early subacute stroke, offering a possible early intervention.
METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, 70 patients with early subacute stroke (7-30 days) were randomized to receive 3 sessions of low-frequency (1 Hz, 1000 pulses at 90% resting motor threshold) rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex (n=35) or sham stimulation (n=35), alongside standard care. The primary outcome was upper-limb spasticity assessed using the modified Modified Ashworth Scale. Secondary outcomes included handgrip strength, muscle power assessed by the Medical Research Council scale, pain assessed by the Visual Analogue Scale, modified Rankin Scale, and Stroke Impact Scale 3.0.
RESULTS: rTMS therapy significantly lowered spasticity scores at 1 and 3 months across all assessed upper-limb joints (P=0.001), improved handgrip strength (P=0.01), and prevented pain (P=0.001). Stroke Impact Scale scores at 1 month showed greater gains in activities of daily living, mobility, hand function, social participation, and recovery in the rTMS group (P=0.001). Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale) was significantly better in the rTMS group (P=0.006) at 3 months. On binary logistic regression, sham stimulation was associated with greater odds of developing spasticity at 1 month (shoulder odds ratio [OR], 8.29 [95% CI, 1.95-35.27], P=0.04; elbow OR, 7.62 [95% CI, 1.69-34.35], P=0.08; wrist OR, 5.18 [95% CI, 1.60-16.78], P=0.06). At 3 months, sham stimulation remained predictive, with higher odds of spasticity at the shoulder (OR, 15.3 [95% CI, 8.26-28.43]), elbow (OR, 13.43 [95% CI, 3.94-45.78]), wrist (OR, 19.9 [95% CI, 4.9-80.96]), and fingers (OR, 26.25 [95% CI, 5.19-132.87], all P=0.001). Minor adverse events like headache and light-headedness were observed in 5 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-frequency rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex significantly prevented spasticity, improved motor recovery, reduced pain, improved functional outcomes and quality of life in early subacute stroke, supporting its role as a promising adjunctive therapy in early stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: Fulminant pancreatic encephalopathy with brain edema and herniation in severe hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis: a case report.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic encephalopathy (PE) is a rare but potentially devastating neurological complication of severe acute pancreatitis. Its manifestations range from confusion and agitation to seizures, coma, and cerebral edema, often making the diagnosis challenging due to its overlap with other causes of encephalopathy. We report a 23-year-old woman with hypertriglyceridemia-induced acute pancreatitis who rapidly progressed to severe acute pancreatitis with multiorgan failure. Within 48 h of admission, she developed agitation, seizure-like activity, and coma. Neuroimaging demonstrated diffuse cerebral and cerebellar edema, features of elevated intracranial pressure, cerebellar tonsillar herniation, and extensive restricted diffusion. After evaluation of alternative etiologies, the neurological deterioration was attributed to PE. Despite aggressive medical management, including insulin therapy, renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and hyperosmolar therapy, she did not show any signs of neurological recovery. This case demonstrates that PE may rarely progress to malignant cerebral edema and tonsillar herniation. New neuropsychiatric manifestations in patients with severe acute pancreatitis should prompt urgent neurological assessment and early neuroimaging whenever clinically feasible.

papers.title: Epilepsy genetics in Africa: a systematic review.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While our understanding of genetic epilepsies is growing, data from Africa remain scant. In this study, we reviewed the profile of epilepsy genetics in Africa.
METHODS: We searched for studies in PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online up to December 2025 using a combination of terms related to "epilepsy", "genetics", and "Africa", and extracted data including phenotype and genetic diagnostics.
RESULTS: Seventy-eight studies from 12 countries met our criteria, encompassing 1,858 individuals (1,339 unaffected, 519 affected) from 384 families. The vast majority of families were reported from three countries, Egypt (144/384, 37.5%), South Africa (76/384, 19.8%), and Morocco (60/384, 15.6%). Generalized epilepsy was the most common presentation (30.5%), followed by focal (18.5%), and unspecified (10.4%). Exome sequencing was used in 71.8% of studies and functional validation was performed in 17.9% of studies (n = 14/78), including cell-based models (12.8%, n = 10/78) and animal models (5.1%, n = 4/78). A total of 165 unique diagnostic genes were reported. Genetic heterogeneity was high, with only 12 genes shared across three or more countries. Of the 384 families, 76.3% (n = 293/384) had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, with the remaining 23.7% (n = 91/384) having VUSs in genes consistent with the seizure phenotype. Six founder variants accounted for 10.7% of the families, 62.0% of variants were novel at the time of reporting, and 67.8% were classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Consanguinity was 45.6% with autosomal recessive the most common inheritance pattern (49.5%).
CONCLUSION: This study highlights substantial clinical and genetic heterogeneity of epilepsy in Africa with population-specific founder variants. Notably, only a limited number of African countries (12/54) have published on molecular diagnostics for epilepsy. The data suggest the potential for significant discoveries yet to be made but also point to ongoing disparities in the availability of genomic testing.

papers.title: Pediatric psychotropic prescribing and polypharmacy, 2019-2022: a retrospective electronic health record study in Qatar.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world evidence on pediatric psychotropic prescribing and polypharmacy in Gulf health systems remains limited. Characterizing medication-class patterns and multi-class prescribing is essential for medication safety surveillance in children and adolescents. This study examined psychotropic prescribing, potential polypharmacy, and recorded medication combinations among children and adolescents using public-sector electronic health records in Qatar.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study used electronic health record data from Hamad Medical Corporation and the Primary Health Care Corporation, Qatar's principal public healthcare providers, from January 2019 to December 2022. Children and adolescents aged 0-17 years with at least one psychotropic prescription were included. Medications were classified as antidepressants, antipsychotics, anxiolytics, mood stabilizers, or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) medications. Potential cross-class polypharmacy was assessed as the recording of two or more medication classes per patient during the study period; available duration information did not permit confirmation of concurrent exposure. Logistic regression examined patient-level associations with this outcome.
RESULTS: The dataset included 2,941 eligible prescription records corresponding to 2,221 unique patients. The proportion of prescriptions for ADHD medications decreased from 28.7% in 2019 to 13.7% in 2022, whereas the proportion assigned to anxiolytics increased from 26.0% to 37.5%. ADHD medications predominated among prescriptions for children aged 5-11 years, while antidepressants and antipsychotics predominated among those for adolescents aged 12-17 years. The potential-polypharmacy criterion was met by 322 patients (14.5%), reaching 21.6% among adolescents. In a gender-adjusted model restricted to patients aged 1-17 years, each additional year of age was associated with higher odds of meeting the criterion (adjusted OR 1.13, 95% CI 1.10-1.16). After excluding patients with prescription-linked seizure disorder or cerebral palsy, the corresponding proportion was 16.96% (259/1,527). Among patients meeting the criterion, antidepressant-antipsychotic and ADHD medication-antipsychotic pairs were most frequent; methylphenidate-risperidone was the most common recorded individual-drug pair.
CONCLUSIONS: This study characterizes pediatric psychotropic prescribing and potential polypharmacy in Qatar's public healthcare records and helps address the limited regional evidence from Gulf health systems. The observed patterns identify potential medication-safety surveillance priorities, particularly among adolescents and patients with antipsychotic-containing medication histories. Further assessment incorporating exposure duration and clinical outcomes is needed to establish concurrency and clinical significance.

papers.title: Admission patterns and clinical management of rare diseases in 46 pediatric intensive care units across China: a multicenter survey.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the admission status of pediatric patients with rare diseases in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) across China, to provide an empirical basis for optimizing critical care management, resource allocation, and healthcare policy development for rare pediatric diseases.
METHODS: An online questionnaire survey was administered to gather cross-sectional data on the admission, diagnosis, treatment, and resource requirements of pediatric patients with rare diseases. A total of 65 questionnaires were returned from all invited member institutions of the Pediatric Critical Care Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association across 30 provinces/municipalities; after exclusion of invalid questionnaires, 46 PICUs across 20 Chinese provincial-level regions constituted the final analytic sample. Data collection covered January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024. Descriptive and comparative statistical analyses were performed on the valid data.
RESULTS: A total of 46 PICUs were included in the final analysis. In 2024, these PICUs admitted 1,765 pediatric patients with rare diseases, accounting for a median of 3.8% of PICU admissions across centers (range 2.1%-6.5%); the pooled proportion was 6.4% (2,231/34,625). The admitted cases covered 89 disorders (43.0%) listed in the National Rare Disease Catalogs of China. Inherited metabolic disorders (48.3%,95% CI: 45.2-51.4%) and neurological disorders (37.6%,95% CI: 34.6-40.6%) were the predominant disease categories, with children aged <3 years accounting for 43.7% of all cases. Most patients were admitted to the PICU due to status epilepticus, respiratory failure, and metabolic crises, indicating high demand for critical care interventions. The overall median time to diagnosis was 30 days; only 26.1% of centers were able to establish a diagnosis within 1 week. The clinical utilization rate of orphan drugs remained markedly low, with exorbitant medication costs and inadequate national health insurance coverage reported as the primary barriers. Healthcare institutions urgently identified the need for enhanced orphan drug accessibility, the establishment of dedicated diagnostic and assistance funds, and accelerated national insurance inclusion.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric rare diseases frequently manifest during infancy and early childhood with acute, life-threatening presentations requiring PICU admission. Currently, clinical management faces substantial bottlenecks, including prolonged diagnostic delays and restricted accessibility to orphan drugs. National-level coordination is urgently required to construct rapid diagnostic green channels, strengthen medication support programs, and optimize the hierarchical healthcare delivery network.

papers.title: Neurologic outcomes following intubation with non-depolarizing vs. depolarizing paralytics in status epilepticus: a target trial emulation.
papers.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Significant controversy exists regarding the optimal pharmacologic approach for endotracheal intubation in patients suffering from status epilepticus (SE).Study Aims: To evaluate post-hospitalization neurologic sequelae and other patient-centered outcomes in SE patients receiving neuromuscular blockers (NMBs). We hypothesized that ability to more rapidly reassess neurologic exam with depolarizing-NMBs (D-NMBs) would mediate improved neurologic outcomes compared to non-depolarizing-NMBs (ND-NMBs).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We analyzed a cohort of SE patients in a large, quaternary academic system from May 2000 to March 2024. Measured confounders were addressed using propensity score methods and inverse probability of treatment weighting. 480 qualifying adults across closely-affiliated health system hospitals undergoing their first intubation for suspected SE with documented paralytic choice were identified via proprietary institutional database using the key search phrase "status epilepticus" in emergency medicine notes. (Exposure: Paralytic selection during rapid sequence intubation - intervention (D-NMB) vs. control (ND-NMB)). As a surrogate towards functional neurologic outcomes, need for "escalation in level of care" at hospital discharge was assessed as primary outcome of interest. Secondary outcomes included major hyperkalemia-related events (ventricular or pulseless arrhythmias) and 30-day survival.
RESULTS: D-NMB use relative to ND-NMB use was associated with increased odds of escalation in level of care upon discharge (30.4% vs. 24.4%, odds ratio [OR] 1.35, 95% CI 1.01-1.81) in addition to decreased odds of home disposition upon hospital discharge (61.7% vs. 69.6%, OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.54-0.94). There was no difference in life-threatening peri-intubation cardiac events such as ventricular or pulseless arrhythmias (0.6% vs. 0.8%, p=0.64).
CONCLUSIONS: Across 480 SE patients, ND-NMBs were associated with lower need for escalation in level of care upon hospital discharge compared to D-NMBs.

papers.title: Surgical and survival outcomes of hemispheric low-grade glioma in Ethiopia: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outcome data for hemispheric low-grade glioma from resource-limited settings remain limited. This study describes surgical, seizure, and survival outcomes among patients treated at two tertiary centers in Ethiopia.
OBJECTIVE: To describe surgical, seizure, and survival outcomes and explore factors associated with overall survival among patients undergoing surgery for hemispheric low-grade glioma.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent surgery for hemispheric low-grade glioma at two tertiary hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, between January 2015 and December 2020. Demographic, clinical, radiologic, operative, histopathologic, treatment, and follow-up data were analyzed. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Associations with survival were explored using univariable Cox proportional hazards analyses. Given the small number of events, survival-factor analyses were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: Thirty-four patients constituted the clinical cohort, with a median age of 39 years. Gross-total resection was performed in 23 (67.6%) patients. Thirty-one patients had sufficient information for time-to-event analysis, among whom 13 deaths were observed. Kaplan-Meier estimated overall survival was 96.7% at 1 year, 67.2% at 2 years, and 53.5% at 3 years. No patients remained under observation at 60 months; therefore, a 5-year survival estimate was not reported. In exploratory univariable analyses, age>40 years, contrast enhancement, and subtotal resection were associated with higher mortality, whereas recorded postoperative chemoradiation was associated with lower mortality. Estimates were imprecise, with wide confidence intervals. Among 23 patients with documented postoperative seizure outcomes, 16 (69.6%) achieved Engel class I status.
CONCLUSION: This multicenter cohort provides real-world surgical and survival data for hemispheric low-grade glioma care in Ethiopia. Several clinical and treatment characteristics were associated with survival, but the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, missing data, and absence of molecular classification preclude definitive conclusions regarding independent prognostic effects. Larger prospective studies incorporating contemporary molecular diagnostics and standardized longitudinal follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Magnetic seizure therapy (MST) is an emerging convulsive treatment for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) with efficacy comparable to electroconvulsive therapy and superior cognitive safety. However, its neurophysiological mechanisms-particularly those underlying conflict monitoring and response inhibition-remain unclear. Frontal midline theta-band activity indexes anterior cingulate-prefrontal cognitive-control activity and may reflect inefficient neural processing in depression.
METHODS: In this open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with TRD (16 female; mean age 20.89 ± 8.16 years; 10 of the 19 participants were minors) received 6-12 MST sessions using 100-Hz double-cone coil stimulation targeting bilateral F3/F4 frontal regions. Clinical assessments, including the 24-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-24), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), and 64-channel Go/Nogo task-based electroencephalography (EEG), were performed before and after treatment. EEG outcome measures included event-related potentials (N2/P3), time-frequency power (theta/beta), microstate dynamics, and theta-beta cross-frequency coupling.
RESULTS: Following MST, patients showed significant reductions in depressive symptoms (HAMD: 40.53 ± 10.25 to 22.53 ± 11.21; MADRS: 35.68 ± 8.84 to 20.68 ± 11.12). Response rates ranged from 42.1% to 57.9%. Behavioral data could not be formally analyzed due to incomplete data storage. At an uncorrected threshold, total Nogo-related theta-band activity (4-7 Hz) at Fz and FCz was lower after treatment; however, these effects did not survive FDR correction. ERP amplitudes did not change significantly. Exploratory microstate analysis showed nominal changes in Map4 AUC during Go processing and Map2 duration during Nogo processing; none survived FDR correction. These parameters should not be interpreted as reflecting changes in neural activation or inhibitory preparation. No significant changes were observed in theta-beta cross-frequency coupling or Go-condition theta power.
DISCUSSION: These preliminary findings suggest that MST was associated with short-term symptom improvement and lower total Nogo-related theta-band activity at an uncorrected threshold. Because no control group, complete behavioral data, normative comparison, Time × Condition interaction, or EEG-clinical association was available, these findings cannot establish causal mechanisms, condition specificity, improved neural efficiency, or biomarker utility. Replication in adequately powered controlled studies with complete behavioral and longitudinal clinical measures is required.

papers.title: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, bispecific antibodies, and multiple myeloma: a case report and systematic review of the literature.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have transformed outcomes in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) but carry a substantial, sustained infectious burden, including rare cases of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML).
METHODS: We present an index case of a patient with RRMM treated with BsAbs diagnosed with PML complicated by immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (PML-IRIS) and perform a systematic review of the literature contextualizing this case among all published reports of PML and PML-IRIS following BsAb therapy in multiple myeloma (MM).
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 65-year-old woman with triple-class-refractory λ light-chain MM who was sequentially treated with the anti-B-cell membrane antigen (BCMA)×CD3 BsAb elranatamab and, subsequently, the anti-GPRC5D×CD3 BsAb talquetamab. During the second cycle of talquetamab, she developed rapidly progressive confusion, visual disturbance, and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Cerebrospinal fluid JC virus (JCV) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was negative on two occasions despite a clinical and radiographic course highly suggestive of PML; brain biopsy confirmed PML-IRIS. Despite talquetamab discontinuation, IVIG, mirtazapine, and compassionate-use nivolumab, the patient achieved only transient neurological stabilization and died 2 months after presentation.
RESULTS: A systematic review of the literature identified 16 additional sources describing 29 patients with PML or PML-IRIS following BsAb therapy for MM, confirmed on full-text review to represent distinct individuals with no duplication between reports. BCMA-directed constructs accounted for most implicated agents, and talquetamab was implicated only in patients with prior or concurrent BCMA-directed exposure. PML-IRIS was documented in two of these patients and could not be excluded in a third. Despite uniformly supportive management, PML-attributable mortality was 89% (25/28) among patients with a definitive reported outcome, including the index case.
CONCLUSION: PML, and PML-IRIS specifically, is an emerging, likely class-level complication of BsAb therapy in MM. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for neuroimaging and CSF JCV testing. These findings should be interpreted in light of the substantial clinical benefit that BsAbs provide in this heavily pretreated population.

papers.title: A case of massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate overdose mimicking brain death.
papers.abstract: A 36-year-old female was brought into hospital following a massive overdose of 100 ml of gamma-hydroxybutyrate. Unlike prior case reports where ethanol was a co-ingestant with gamma-hydroxybutyrate or its precursor, gamma-hydroxybutyrate was believed to have been the only substance ingested in this case. The patient developed a severe and persistent high anion gap metabolic acidosis and required continuous renal replacement therapy. The patient developed fixed and dilated pupils early on in her clinical course and was found to have a transient loss of most brainstem reflexes on clinical examination, thus mimicking brain death. She also developed generalised tonic-clonic seizures and received midazolam and levetiracetam for seizure control. She was successfully extubated after 5 days on mechanical ventilation and was discharged home on day 11 with no neurological deficits.

papers.title: Anticholinergic Burden in People With Intellectual Disability.
papers.journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with intellectual disability (ID) experience high rates of multimorbidity and psychotropic prescribing, placing them at greater risk of anticholinergic burden (ACB), which has been associated with adverse cognitive and physical health outcomes. However, data on ACB among people with an ID attending specialist mental health services remain limited.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted for all adults with an ID (N = 159) attending a specialist mental health service. Demographic, clinical and prescribing data were extracted from clinical records. ACB was determined using the online ACB Calculator. Rates of psychiatric and physical health comorbidity and prescribing were examined.
RESULTS: Elevated ACB was common, with 65% of service users recording clinically significant scores. ACB was higher in females and those in residential services and positively correlated with age and total medication burden but did not differ according to ID level. Polypharmacy was present in 57% of service users, and antipsychotics were the most frequently prescribed psychotropic medication (82%). Individuals with Down syndrome demonstrated lower ACB scores than those without. In multivariate analyses, the number of prescribed medications and antipsychotics independently predicted clinically significant ACB.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with an ID attending specialist mental health services experience substantial exposure to anticholinergic medications within the context of multimorbidity and polypharmacy. Elevated ACB appears to be driven by overall medication burden and psychotropic prescribing, particularly antipsychotic use. Routine assessment of ACB alongside individual-reported experiences and clinician-rated outcomes should form part of regular medication review processes to identify potentially modifiable prescribing risks and support safer pharmacological management. Future research should examine whether interventions that reduce ACB improve subjective, clinician-rated and broader health outcomes in ID.

papers.title: Epileptiform Discharges in Seizure-Free Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and the Role of Antiseizure Medications.
papers.journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of epileptiform discharges (EPDs) in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) without clinical seizures, assess autism severity using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition (CARS-2), and reassess the children after treatment with antiseizure medications (ASMs).
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective cohort study. Place and Duration of the Study: Four autism centres in Duhok City, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, from August 2024 to August 2025.
METHODOLOGY: Fifty children with seizure-free ASD (aged 2.5-18 years) underwent clinical evaluation, electroencephalography (EEG) recording, and severity assessment using CARS-2. Children with EPDs were offered ASMs according to EEG pattern and clinical profile. EEG and CARS-2 assessments were repeated after 6 months. Data were analysed using SPSS version 31.0. Descriptive statistics were presented as means ± standard deviations for continuous variables and frequencies with percentages for categorical variables. For group comparisons, independent t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for small samples were used. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: EPDs were detected in 24 participants (48%). EPDs were focal in 19 cases (79.16) and generalised in 5 cases (20.83). Adherence to ASMs after 6 months was observed in 9 cases (37.5 %). All adherent participants demonstrated EEG improvement and significant reductions in total CARS-2 scores (p = 0.001). Improvements were also observed in the following domains: emotional response (p = 0.023), body use (p = 0.024), activity level (p = 0.026), visual response (p = 0.040), taste, smell and touch (p = 0.057), and general impression of ASD (p = 0.026). Adverse effects were reported in 6/15 (40%) participants whom started ASMs, primarily behavioural.
CONCLUSION: EPDs are common in children with ASD, even in the absence of clinical seizures. When ASMs were used consistently, EEG improvements were observed, and ASD severity scores on the CARS-2 were reduced.   Key Words: Anti-seizure medications, Autism spectrum disorder, Electroencephalography, Epileptiform discharges.

papers.title: Clinical characterization and genotype-phenotype correlations in Chilton-Okur-Chung syndrome.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chilton-Okur-Chung neurodevelopmental syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by global developmental delay, variable intellectual disability, behavioral challenges, and structural brain anomalies caused by variants in CDC42BPB. CDC42BPB encodes MRCKβ, a ubiquitously expressed serine/threonine kinase involved in cytoskeletal regulation. The phenotypic spectrum and genotype-phenotype relationships remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We aggregated data from 20 newly identified individuals and 17 previously reported individuals. We analyzed the data for genotype-phenotype correlations according to variant type.
RESULTS: Developmental delay was the most common phenotype, affecting 85% of individuals, with early delays notable in walking and speech. Intellectual disability was observed in 62%. Behavioral diagnoses included autism spectrum disorder (68%) and ADHD (60%). Structural brain abnormalities were present in 48% of cases, predominantly affecting the cerebellum and ventricles. Dysmorphic features were present in 83% of cases. Hypotonia was present in 68%, seizures in 41%, and macrocephaly in 38%. Genotype-phenotype analysis indicated that predicted loss-of-function (LoF) variants were generally associated with milder neurodevelopmental features than missense variants. A male predominance was observed despite this being an autosomal dominant condition, suggesting a possible protective effect in females. Some heterozygous predicted LoF variants were inherited from self-reported unaffected parents or with subtle neurodevelopmental or cardiac features, supporting incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the differences between predicted loss-of-function and missense variants. Future studies assessing biochemical differences in kinase activity and substrate specificity may explain these clinical differences.

papers.title: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency initially diagnosed as acute necrotizing encephalopathy in a child: a case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBP1) deficiency is a rare inherited defect of gluconeogenesis that can cause fasting- or infection-triggered hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and multisystem biochemical disturbances. Acute metabolic crises may produce symmetric deep gray-matter or diffuse cortical abnormalities on neuroimaging, mimicking infection-triggered encephalopathy syndromes such as acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE). We report a school-aged patient whose presentation and early imaging suggested ANE but was ultimately explained by genetically confirmed fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency.
CASE PRESENTATION: A previously healthy 7-year-old girl was found in a coma with ongoing generalized seizures and fever. Her fingerstick glucose was 1.8 mmol/L. Clinical tests showed metabolic acidosis (pH 7.22), significant hyperlactatemia, hyperuricemia, low sodium levels, and high transaminases and lactate dehydrogenase. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed mild bilateral thalamic hyperintensity, with high levels of Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Interleukin-8 (IL-8) in the cerebrospinal fluid, prompting empiric treatment with high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, intrathecal corticosteroids, tocilizumab and intensive supportive care. The patient improved after metabolic correction. A follow-up MRI on day 7 revealed extensive bilateral hemispheric abnormalities atypical for necrotizing encephalopathy. Infectious causes were ruled out. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous c.490G > A (p.Gly164Ser) mutation in the FBP1 gene; both parents were heterozygous, and a sibling was also homozygous. Treatment focused on prompt glucose administration, correcting acidosis, and dietary management. The patient was discharged on day 22 in stable condition, with complete resolution of acute abnormal signals, and remained asymptomatic at six months.
CONCLUSIONS: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency can present beyond infancy and mimic necrotizing encephalopathy. Recognition of severe hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and multisystem abnormalities should prompt immediate metabolic stabilization and targeted genetic testing to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary immunomodulatory therapy.

papers.title: Adjunctive Brivaracetam in Early Treatment Line Combinations: 12-Month Real-World Experience and Impact on Health Outcomes in Adult Patients with Focal Seizures.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postmarketing data for adjunctive brivaracetam (BRV) suggest potential benefit in earlier antiseizure medication (ASM) regimens.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate real-world effectiveness of BRV in earlier ASM therapy lines (over ~12 months) in patients with focal seizures with/without focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures (primary objective) and assess patient characteristics, health outcomes, and tolerability.
METHODS: Prospective, postmarketing, noninterventional study of adjunctive BRV in Europe/Canada (December 2020-January 2024; BRITOBA/EP0103). Selection criteria are adults (≥ 18 years) with history of focal seizures, no prior BRV treatment, and ≤ 3 lifetime (prior/at BRV initiation) ASMs when initiating adjunctive BRV.
RESULTS: A total of 392 patients received ≥ 1 BRV dose (mean age 44.9 years; mean lifetime ASMs 2.0). Of 298 patients, 41.9% were seizure-free for ≥ 6 consecutive months during up to ~12 months' observation. At 12 months, 20.5% of 254 patients were seizure-free from baseline, 75.7% of 292 achieved ≥ 50% focal seizure reduction from baseline, 75.5% of 392 remained on BRV, and 72.0% of 289 and 66.8% of 211 had improved (minimally/much/very much) on Clinical Global Impression of Change and Patient's Global Impression of Change. From baseline to 12 months, Ten-Item Patient-Weighted Quality of Life in Epilepsy Inventory (QOLIE-10-P) total score improved by a mean of 9.9 points (n = 152); Nine-Item Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire for Medication effectiveness, convenience, and global satisfaction scores improved by a mean of 21.6 (n = 144), 6.1 (n = 146), and 19.1 (n = 145) points; Work Productivity and Activity Impairment Questionnaire: General Health scores showed numerical mean improvements in percentages of activity impairment due to health problem (-14.0 [n = 157]), work time missed due to health problem (-12.3 [n = 50]), impairment while working due to health problem (-7.8 [n = 63]), and overall work impairment due to health problem (-9.0 [n = 48]); and the Neurological Disorders Depression Inventory in Epilepsy score improved by a mean of -1.1 points (n = 158). Seizure Severity Questionnaire (questions 5 and 8 only) showed numerically fewer reports of postictal cognitive effects (37.0% of 135 patients versus 63.6% of 308) and improved median seizure severity score (2.0 [n = 124] versus 4.0 points [n = 301]) at 12 months versus baseline. Of 392 patients, 13.8% experienced ≥ 1 drug-related treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE), 9.4% discontinued BRV due to TEAEs.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with focal seizures, BRV in earlier ASM regimens was effective and well tolerated. At 12 months, there were improvements in quality of life, clinical condition, work productivity, and treatment satisfaction.

papers.title: SySCOM: epileptogenic focus localisation using synthetic interictal SPECT images in SISCOM.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interictal SPECT is a critical component of SISCOM analysis for presurgical localisation of epileptogenic regions. However, its clinical reliability can be affected by uncertainty regarding whether the interictal scan is a true representation of a seizure free baseline (i.e., the interictal state). In addition, most patients will also have an interictal FDG PET scan and MRI performed, and it would be useful if the number of scans required could be reduced. This study explores the use of machine learning synthesised interictal SPECT within the SISCOM framework (i.e., SySCOM) as an alternative baseline to the acquired interictal SPECT scan.
METHODS: PET scans from 40 patients with refractory focal epilepsy were used to train a three-dimensional generative adversarial network to synthesise interictal SPECT images. Synthesis performance was evaluated on an independent validation cohort of nine unseen patients using standard image quality metrics (i.e., SSIM, PSNR, RMSE). Both real and synthetic interictal SPECT images were used to generate SISCOM outputs following standard clinical protocols. Five clinicians experienced in the interpretation of SPECT images in epilepsy performed blinded visual localisation of regions of hyperperfusion across 18 predefined anatomical regions. Observer based similarity, agreement, and reproducibility between SISCOM and SySCOM were assessed.
RESULTS: Synthetic interictal SPECT images demonstrated high similarity to real images (mean SSIM = 0.94, mean PSNR = 27.9 dB, mean RMSE = 0.041). Visual localisation based comparison of SISCOM with SySCOM demonstrated good agreement between the methods (Dice score = 70%), with an overall 89% agreement across all subjects and regions. Individual reader agreement between sessions remained high, indicating stable interpretation across image types.
CONCLUSION: Machine learning-generated interictal SPECT can be used to produce SySCOM, which is visually and quantitatively comparable to SISCOM, as confirmed by expert readers. The findings demonstrate consistent localisation patterns, high observer agreement, and stable reader reproducibility. This work addresses uncertainty associated with confirming a true seizure-free baseline during interictal SPECT acquisition. SySCOM can therefore be considered a feasible approach that requires further clinical validation before routine clinical implementation.

papers.title: Radiopharmaceuticals in Molecular Neuroimaging: Food and Drug Administration-Approved Radiotracers.
papers.abstract: FDA-approved PET and SPECT radiopharmaceuticals have transformed neuroimaging practice by allowing direct, in vivo evaluation of cerebral metabolism, perfusion, neurotransmitter systems, and protein aggregates such as amyloid and tau. Their use has increased diagnostic confidence and improved treatment decisions in dementia, movement disorders, epilepsy, and neuro-oncology. In routine care, some approved tracers are used off-label, guided by available evidence, to expand their clinical utility. PET offers superior spatial resolution, whereas SPECT is more accessible and cost-effective. Used together, these imaging tools support earlier, more confident diagnoses and improve patient outcomes.

Nuclear brain imaging studies provide functional and molecular data that can be crucial in the identifying of epileptogenic areas of the brain. Brain imaging data obtained from perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and interictal PET and PET/MR imaging can inform invasive monitoring with stereotactic electroencephalography and guide the performance of destructive surgical interventions.

papers.title: A successful clozapine rechallenge in a patient with treatment-resistant schizophrenia:A case report.
papers.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clozapine is the gold standard treatment for treatment-resistant schizophrenia;however, discontinuation may be necessary because of hematologic side effects such as neutropenia. This report describes a case in which clozapine was reintroduced along with lithium after neutropenia, resulting in a favorable outcome.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old woman with a 16-year history of schizophrenia remained stable on clozapine (300 mg/day) after failing to respond to multiple antipsychotics. However, clozapine was discontinued when neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count, 1,414/μL) developed during viral-like symptoms. Subsequently, her psychiatric symptoms recurred, and other medications were ineffective. Therefore, clozapine was reinitiated in combination with lithium. Hematologic abnormalities did not recur, and behavioral symptoms improved markedly. After increasing the dose of clozapine to 450 mg/day and that of lithium to 800 mg/day, she experienced a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. However, after reducing the dose of these medications, no recurrence occurred, and her condition remained stable.
CONCLUSION: Based on the revised Japanese clozapine monitoring guidelines, the reintroduction of clozapine after viral neutropenia is possible through multidisciplinary collaboration. Lithium co-administration may have contributed to hematologic stability by promoting granulocyte production. However, caution is warranted because of the increased seizure risk, and careful monitoring of neurological side effects is essential. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 566-568, August, 2026.

papers.title: Recurrent hip dislocation in an adult patient with trisomy 21: a case report.
papers.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip instability in individuals with trisomy 21 commonly presents as habitual dislocation or progressive subluxation, whereas recurrent dislocation is extremely rare. Only a few reports have described recurrent hip dislocation in skeletally mature patients. Furthermore, the role of acetabular osteotomy remains unclear.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 22-year-old man with trisomy 21 who developed recurrent posterior hip dislocation following a seizure-related fall. Radiographs and computed tomography revealed severe acetabular dysplasia (Tönnis angle, 28º;acetabular version, 0°) with femoral anteversion of 57°. Navigation-assisted eccentric rotational acetabular osteotomy was performed;however, a posterior column fracture occurred intraoperatively. Although postoperative radiographs demonstrated improved acetabular orientation with a Tönnis angle of 3º and acetabular version of 15°, posterior subluxation recurred 6 months after surgery. The posterior column fracture healed without displacement, but residual ligamentous laxity and femoral deformity likely contributed to persistent instability. Despite radiographic progression of osteoarthritis at 1 year, the patient remained asymptomatic.
CONCLUSION: Recurrent hip dislocation in adults with trisomy 21 typically results from a multifactorial combination of acetabular dysplasia, femoral anteversion, and ligamentous laxity. When acetabular osteotomy is considered, careful assessment of posterior column thickness and meticulous osteotomy planning are essential to avoid intraoperative fracture and optimize postoperative stability. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 519-524, August, 2026.

papers.title: [Epilepsy and Alcohol].
papers.journal: Brain and nerve = Shinkei kenkyu no shinpo
papers.abstract: The association between alcohol consumption and epilepsy is both complex and clinically significant. Acute alcohol intake suppresses central nervous system activity, while abrupt cessation of chronic heavy drinking can trigger rebound neuronal hyperexcitability, resulting in alcohol withdrawal seizures. In patients with epilepsy, heavy or binge drinking may increase seizure risk, particularly when concurrent with sleep deprivation, poor antiseizure medication adherence, dehydration, nutritional disturbances, or metabolic abnormalities. Alcohol-related seizures must be distinguished from alcohol withdrawal seizures, seizures associated with underlying epilepsy, and acute symptomatic seizures attributable to other causes, such as head trauma, cerebrovascular disease, infection, and metabolic disturbances. Therefore, clinical assessments should consider the amount and pattern of alcohol consumption, interval between the last drink and seizure onset, withdrawal symptoms, seizure characteristics, epilepsy history, medication adherence, and other potential precipitants. Benzodiazepines are the mainstay of acute management for alcohol withdrawal seizures, with treatment aiming to control withdrawal syndrome and prevent severe complications, in addition to preventing recurrent seizures. Although heavy alcohol consumption is associated with an increased risk of seizures and epilepsy, evidence regarding the effects of low-level alcohol consumption remains limited. Individualized risk assessment and counseling are essential in clinical practice.

papers.title: [Effects of Alcohol on the Central Nervous System].
papers.journal: Brain and nerve = Shinkei kenkyu no shinpo
papers.abstract: Alcohol affects the central nervous system through acute and chronic mechanisms. The acute effects include intoxication and blackouts, whereas abrupt cessation or reduction in alcohol intake after chronic excessive consumption may result in alcohol-withdrawal syndrome, seizures, and alcohol-induced psychotic symptoms. Chronic excessive alcohol consumption may cause cognitive impairment and structural changes in the brain through direct neurotoxicity, nutritional deficiency, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress. Neuroimaging studies have shown that alcohol use disorder is associated with reduced brain volume, and it may accelerate age-related brain changes, particularly in the frontal regions. Alcohol use disorder is also associated with an increased risk of dementia, particularly early-onset dementia. In contrast to progressive neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease, alcohol-related cognitive impairment can partially improve with sustained abstinence or reduced alcohol consumption. Alcohol-related dementia is a clinically important but incompletely defined condition, and its diagnostic criteria, underlying pathophysiology, relationship to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, and nosological status, are subject to ongoing debate.

papers.title: Individualized and stereotypical seizure semiology in a porcine model of post-traumatic epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Large-animal models of traumatic brain injury may yield translatable data on epileptogenesis, given their similarities in anatomy, brain size, and immune systems to humans. Adult male and female swine received bilateral cortical impact (N = 16) or sham surgery (N = 6) and were screened for convulsions via video-EEG for up to one year. Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) was defined as 2 seizures after 1-week post-injury. Eight out of sixteen pigs (50%) receiving bilateral cortical impact developed PTE, with an average latent period of 5 months (± 3.7). Seizures (N = 190) began focally, sometimes with motor onset including automatisms, before becoming generalized, with tonic-clonic or tonic convulsions. We defined a library differentiating peri-ictal behaviors (N = 31) from rhythmic/odd behaviors typical in healthy pigs (N = 12). Seizures had an average of 6.95 behaviors per seizure (max 26) lasting an average of 1.8 min (max 7.9). For seizures comprised of multiple convulsive episodes, the first convulsion had a greater number of peri-ictal behaviors than subsequent convulsions (P < 0.001). The array of peri-ictal behaviors displayed was moderately pig-specific, with many behaviors consistently observed across seizures. The seizure frequency detected was 0.43/day. This large-brain model of PTE exhibits a variable period of epileptogenesis, a substantial rate of PTE, and an expansive repertoire of ictal behaviors. This first description of semiology in this species will serve as a guide for other porcine epilepsy models. Biofidelic models of PTE are expected to increase our understanding of the pathophysiology, enabling the identification and testing of therapeutics that translate into human patients.

papers.title: Disease-modifying therapies in development for post-traumatic epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a chronic neurological disorder that develops following traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition affecting nearly 69 million people worldwide. PTE accounts for 20% of acquired epilepsies and is characterized by spontaneous recurrent seizures and long-term neurological deficits. Current antiseizure medications primarily suppress early seizures but do not prevent epileptogenesis or improve neurological dysfunction. This review critically evaluates the current landscape of disease-modifying therapies for PTE with an emphasis on pathophysiological basis, therapeutic pipeline and challenges in developing antiepileptogenic drugs for preventing PTE and improving long-term neurological outcomes after TBI. Epileptogenesis following TBI is driven by dynamic interactions among neuronal, glial, vascular, immune, metabolic, and epigenetic pathways that evolve from the acute injury phase through the latent period to chronic epilepsy. Consequently, therapeutic interventions differ in optimal timing and target objectives of acute neuroprotection, prevention of epileptogenesis, or modification of established epilepsy and its comorbidities. Promising disease-modifying approaches include epigenetic modulators, anti-inflammatory & immunomodulatory agents, JAK-STAT inhibitors, mTOR inhibitors, antioxidant & mitochondrial-targeted therapies, tau-directed interventions, adenosine augmentation, neurosteroids, and regenerative cell-based therapies. Among these, epigenetic therapy targeting histone deacetylases has emerged as a particularly attractive strategy. Pharmacological inhibition of histone deacetylase has demonstrated robust disease-modifying effects in experimental PTE by normalizing aberrant histone deacetylase activity, suppressing neuroinflammation, reducing seizure burden, and attenuating biomarkers of epileptogenic progression. Despite multiple approaches in development, no therapy has yet demonstrated clinical efficacy for preventing human PTE. Major translation barriers include the heterogeneity of PTE, limitations of experimental models, inconsistent biomarker validation, and challenges in clinical studies. Future progress will require standardized paradigms, rigorous preclinical evaluation, biomarker-guided clinical trials, and optimization of disease-modifying therapies capable of preventing epilepsy and improving long-term neurological outcomes after brain injury.

papers.title: Status Epilepticus in a Patient Prescribed Theophylline: A Case Report.
papers.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Seizures are a frequent reason for emergency department (ED) evaluation, and new-onset events carry a wide differential in which medication toxicity can be overlooked. Toxicity from seldomly prescribed drugs, such as theophylline, can be particularly challenging to recognize because they can cause nonspecific adverse effects, including palpitations, nausea, vomiting, and seizures. Although theophylline use was widespread in the 1980s, current prescribing patterns are unknown. Nevertheless, theophylline toxicity continues to result in ED visits and poison center calls. Because adverse effects may be acute or chronic, identifying theophylline toxicity remains difficult.
CASE REPORT: A 74-year-old woman presented to the ED with status epilepticus. After thorough history and extensive medical work-up, medication toxicity was suspected as the cause of her seizures. Upon further investigation, the patient was found to have theophylline toxicity. Prompt treatment was initiated resulting in cessation of seizures, highlighting the importance of considering medication toxicity in geriatric patients with new-onset seizures.
CONCLUSION: Theophylline toxicity can present with vague, multisystem symptoms, with status epilepticus being one of its most severe complications. Rapid identification of the underlying toxic etiology is essential to guide treatment and stop the seizures. Moreover, clinical suspicion should be elevated in the geriatric population related to frequent polypharmacy. In this case, confirming the medication history with a family member raised concerns for medication misuse, enabling timely intervention. Although rarely prescribed, physicians should counsel patients on the risks and adverse effects of theophylline and emphasize close monitoring.

papers.title: Cauda Equina Syndrome Secondary to Seizure-Induced Spinal Fracture During Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy carries a risk of central nervous system oxygen toxicity, which can result in seizures. Seizure-induced spinal fractures are uncommon complications that occur during generalized convulsive activity. While often benign, lumbar vertebral body burst fractures may result in cauda equina syndrome. Additionally, patients with beta-thalassemia may have decreased bone mineral density due to ineffective erythropoiesis and bone marrow expansion increasing the risk for pathologic and traumatic fractures.
CASE REPORT: A 35-year-old man with beta-thalassemia major presented to the emergency department after a witnessed, first-time generalized tonic-clonic seizure during hyperbaric oxygen therapy for chronic venous ulcers. Initial evaluation revealed severe low back pain and midline lumbar tenderness. Computed tomography revealed an acute third lumbar vertebra (L3) burst fracture with retropulsion. The patient rapidly developed progressive right lower-extremity weakness and acute urinary retention. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed 70% loss of height of L3, severe thecal sac stenosis at L2-L3 and L3-L4, and a ventral dural hematoma resulting in stenosis at L4-L5. The patient was diagnosed with cauda equina syndrome and underwent emergent neurosurgical decompression.
CONCLUSION: This case represents a rare convergence of multiple complications: central nervous system oxygen toxicity during hyperbaric oxygen therapy, seizure-induced lumbar burst fracture with retropulsion, and traumatic cauda equina syndrome in a patient with beta thalassemia. Physicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for vertebral fractures and monitor for evolving neurological deficits when managing the patient with acute back pain following seizure activity.

papers.title: Is it possible to vaccinate AI against bias? An exploratory study in epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may respond differently to clinical vignettes containing different patient descriptions. This exploratory proof-of-concept study examined whether an instruction to reconsider irrelevant information changed such responses in epilepsy. One diagnostic and one treatment vignette each had an affluent and a disadvantaged composite profile, differing jointly in sex and social descriptors. The reported design comprised six models, two prompt conditions, and ten repetitions per cell (480 responses). We retained the original binary reference-answer rubric and recalculated descriptive results from the reported aggregate table. Diagnostic accuracy under this rubric increased from 43/120 (35.8%) to 66/120 (55.0%), while the signed pooled accuracy gap decreased from 45.0 to 26.7 percentage points. Treatment accuracy increased from 61/120 (50.8%) to 75/120 (62.5%), while the pooled gap decreased from 25.0 to 8.3 points. Mean absolute model-level gaps decreased from 45.0 to 30.0 points for diagnosis and from 35.0 to 11.7 points for treatment. Individual models showed improvement, deterioration, or unchanged performance. Retained response collections and scoring records do not permit complete verification of all reported runs or model versions. These findings illustrate a method for examining prompt sensitivity; they do not isolate socioeconomic bias or establish a clinically effective debiasing intervention. Simple prompt-based interventions may offer a practical strategy to mitigate AI bias in epilepsy care.

papers.title: EXPAND-ing evidence-based epilepsy self-management into clinical settings.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This is a scale-up report on the SMART (Self-management for people with epilepsy and a history of negative health events) epilepsy self-management (ESM) program.
METHODS: Engagement in SMART was assessed via session attendance (maximum of 8). Outcomes included the 10-item Quality of Life in Epilepsy (QOLIE-10), Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Neurological DisordersDepression Inventory for Epilepsy (NDDI-E) and past 30-day seizure frequency.
RESULTS: 153 PWE were referred to ESM, mean age 37.6 (SD 12.8). Average attendance for PWE who attended ≥ 1 session (N = 115) was 5.8 (SD 2.6). There were no significant pre/post changes for QOLIE-10, NDDI-E, GAD-7, PHQ-9 or past 30-day seizure counts. Exploratory analysis of clinically relevant subgroups found PWE with PHQ-9 ≥ 10 at baseline (N = 27), had significant improvement pre/post SMART with means of 15.0 (SD 4.5) and 11.7 (SD 5.1), respectively (p = 0.001), those with GAD-7 ≥ 10 at baseline (N = 31) had significant improvement pre/post SMART with means of 14.4 (SD 3.2) and 11.2 (SD 3.8), respectively (p = 0.001) and those in the lowest quartile of QOLIE-10 scores (N = 16) had significant improvement pre/post SMART with means of 3.8 (SD 0.5) and 3.4 (SD 0.8), respectively.
DISCUSSION: This analysis from a real-world, non-research study sample suggests scaling up ESM in an epilepsy-care clinical setting appears feasible, acceptable to PWE, and can improve outcomes for PWE with depression, anxiety and suboptimal quality of life. Future work needs to address barriers to generalizability.

papers.title: Effect of Campi the Seahorse video interventions on improving knowledge about epilepsy and reducing stigmatizing beliefs in primary school pupils.
papers.abstract: Children with epilepsy continue to face stigma and peer exclusion in school settings, highlighting the need for effective age-appropriate educational interventions. This study evaluated the effects at 6-month follow-up of Episodes 3 + 4 of the Campi the Seahorse educational video series in improving epilepsy knowledge and reducing stigma among primary school pupils aged 9-12. A total of 94 pupils received the Campi 3 + 4 intervention and completed measures of epilepsy knowledge and stigma at baseline and at a 6-month follow-up. Their outcomes were compared with data from 197 pupils who had previously received the Campi 1 + 2 video (n = 111) or a Campi-based read story intervention (n = 86). In the Campi 3 + 4 group, epilepsy knowledge increased significantly from baseline to follow-up (M = 7.14, SD = 2.42 vs. M = 9.36, SD = 3.37, p < 0.001, d = 0.75), with substantial improvements in knowledge of brain function, first aid, and seizure manifestations. Epilepsy-related stigma also decreased significantly (M = 42.14, SD = 14.66 vs. M = 38.11, SD = 14.88, p = 0.011, d = 0.27), with exploratory item-level changes in work-related prejudice and perceived incapability. ANCOVA controlling for baseline scores showed no significant differences in knowledge at the 6-month follow-up across the three interventions (p = 0.243). After adjustment for baseline stigma scores, the overall difference in stigma scores among the three intervention groups was statistically significant (p = 0.040), with the Campi 3 + 4 group showing the lowest adjusted mean. However, the multiplicity-adjusted pairwise comparisons were not significant (p > 0.05). Findings of this non-randomized study suggest that Campi Episodes 3 + 4 provide a brief educational intervention associated with improvements in epilepsy knowledge and lower stigma. Their focus on first aid, common misconceptions, and social inclusion may make them a relevant option when implementation of the complete four-episode series is not feasible.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel Nav1.2 inhibitors as antiepileptic agents.
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.2 is a validated target for anticonvulsant therapy, yet Nav1.2 inhibitors remain scarce. To explore the unexplored N-4 position of the [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine scaffold, we designed and synthesized two series of novel derivatives bearing diverse substituents at this position. Their Nav1.2 inhibitory activities were evaluated using FLIPR membrane potential and whole-cell patch-clamp assays, while their anticonvulsant efficacy and neurotoxicity were assessed in MES/ sc-PTZ seizure models and rotarod test, respectively. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis revealed that hydrophobic volume complementarity, rather than aromaticity, is the primary driver of Nav1.2 potency. Compound 3b, bearing a simple n-butyl group at N-4, emerged as the most promising lead, exhibiting moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (88.9% at 30 μM; FLIPR IC50 = 11.55 μM; patch-clamp IC50 = 7.62 μM for the inactivated state) and exceptional in vivo efficacy (ED50 = 9.17 mg/kg, TD50 > 813.40 mg/kg, PI >88.70) in the sc-PTZ model. Compound 3y also demonstrated moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (69.8%, IC50 = 12.19 μM) and potent anticonvulsant activity (ED50 = 13.7 mg/kg, PI >23.1). Patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed that 3b and 3y inhibit the inactivated state of Nav1.2 (IC50 = 7.62 μM and 8.31 μM, respectively) with negligible effect on the resting state. Molecular docking and MD simulations revealed that 3b binds within the Nav1.2 pore via hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and hydrophobic contacts. Tissue distribution studies demonstrated efficient blood-brain barrier penetration (brain-to-plasma ratio of 1.65 at 1 h post-dose). Although 3b showed limited stability in human and rat liver microsomes (T1/2 = 12.20 and 10.65 min, respectively), its potent in vivo efficacy and exceptionally high protective index support its continued optimization and preclinical development as a promising candidate for epilepsy therapy.

papers.title: Frequency of occurrence, signalment, clinicopathologic and imaging findings, and outcomes with nontraumatic spontaneous intracranial hemorrhagic stroke in dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the frequency, clinicopathologic and imaging findings, and outcomes in dogs with spontaneous intra-parenchymal hemorrhagic stroke (sIHS).
ANIMALS: Retrospective study involving 25 dogs.
CLINICAL PRESENTATION: Medical records were reviewed for signalment; neurological, clinicopathologic, and imaging findings; anatomic localization; comorbidities; therapy; and outcome in dogs with sIHS (2010 to 2024). Lesion number, location, and volume were recorded. Outcome was defined as excellent, good, or poor. Frequency was defined out of a contemporaneous population of dogs ≥ 6 years old with an acute presentation of neurological signs.
RESULTS: Affected dogs were older, small- to medium-breed dogs. Dogs often presented for neurological dysfunction reflective of a prosencephalic lesion (19 of 25 dogs) or new-onset seizures (13 of 25 dogs). A single, well-defined hemorrhage within the prosencephalon was commonly observed on MRI. Outcome was frequently excellent. Complete seizure remission was common. Larger lesion volumes were associated with poor outcomes. One dog experienced clinical signs suggestive of an additional sIHS 4 months after the initial stroke. Frequency of sIHS was 25 of 427 dogs (6%) ≥ 6 years old undergoing brain MRI.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: sIHS should be considered in older dogs with an acute onset of prosencephalic dysfunction and/or seizures. Following exclusion of secondary IHS, an excellent long-term outcome may be realized in dogs with sIHS, despite the presence of comorbidities. Short-term anticonvulsant therapy may be necessary. Development of poststroke epilepsy is unlikely. Dogs rarely experience another IHS.

papers.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy in non-NF1 RASopathies: a two-centre retrospective paediatric cohort and scoping review.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in non-NF1 RASopathies through a scoping review and a two-centre paediatric cohort.
METHODS: We searched PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase and Scopus from inception to September 2026 for terms covering non-NF1 RASopathies and epilepsy/seizures. Four reviewers independently screened records and extracted data in duplicate; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Eligible records reported individuals with a non-NF1 RASopathy, seizure onset up to 17 years, and confirmed epilepsy. DRE was defined by ILAE (failure of ≥2 appropriate antiseizure medications [ASMs] at adequate dose). In parallel, we retrospectively identified paediatric patients with genetically confirmed Noonan syndrome (NS) or cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome (CFC) and DRE from two London centres over a five-year period; clinical, EEG and MRI features, ASMs and outcomes were abstracted.
RESULTS: Of 801 records identified across three databases, 435 were screened following deduplication; 48 met inclusion criteria. Across the literature, NS showed lower epilepsy frequency and severity; DRE was uncommon and often associated with structural aetiologies. CFC displayed a severe, polymorphic phenotype with frequent status epilepticus and high DRE rates. Recent evidence also identified subclinical epileptiform activity, including continuous spike-and-wave during sleep, in CFC patients without overt seizures. Our cohort comprised six patients: two NS (variants in BRAF, PTPN11) and four CFC (all MAP2K1). Seizure types included tonic-clonic, focal seizures and infantile spasms; most required multiple ASMs. EEG abnormalities were non-specific. MRI showed heterogeneous findings, including mesial temporal sclerosis, cerebral atrophy, delayed myelination, and hippocampal dysgyria. Neurodevelopmental impairment (including autism spectrum disorder) was common.
CONCLUSIONS: In non-NF1 RASopathies, DRE reflects combined genetic and structural contributors; in CFC, clinical-imaging correlations support a spectrum towards developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Management should consider non-pharmacological options and carefully selected targeted approaches; mechanism-informed choices may be considered where appropriate, acknowledging that the supporting evidence remains observational.

papers.title: Clinical Risk Factors for Suicide in Persons With Epilepsy: A Nationwide Population-Based Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Individuals with epilepsy face an elevated risk of suicide, but risk factors for suicide remain incompletely understood. We conducted a nationwide case-control study in Sweden to investigate clinical characteristics associated with suicide risk in persons with epilepsy.
METHODS: Persons with epilepsy were identified through Swedish nationwide registers, with epilepsy diagnoses validated through medical record review. Cases were individuals who died by suicide between 2006 and 2011, validated through autopsy reports, and controls were derived from the source population using similar validation procedures. Characteristics included epilepsy type, etiology, tonic-clonic seizure (TCS) frequency, antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment, living conditions, and psychiatric comorbidity. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were estimated using conditional logistic regression.
RESULTS: The study included 111 suicide cases and 1,147 controls. Suicide cases had a mean age at epilepsy onset of 20 years, and 35% were female. Alcohol abuse (OR 11.81, 95% CI 6.25-22.30) and other substance abuse (OR 10.71, 95% CI 4.52-25.38) showed stronger associations than depression (OR 2.94, 95% CI 1.56-5.53) and anxiety disorders (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.57-5.44). Living alone was associated with increased risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.58-4.26). Recent TCS showed a dose-response relationship, with the highest risk among individuals experiencing 4-10 TCS in the preceding year (OR 5.01, 95% CI 2.2-11.3). Structural and unknown epilepsy etiologies were associated with elevated risk (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.0-9.5 and OR 8.80, 95% CI 2.9-27.1, respectively). ASM treatment was associated with lower suicide risk (monotherapy OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95; polytherapy OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.1-0.5), and nonadherence was associated with higher risk (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.8-5.1).
DISCUSSION: This study identified a distinct risk profile for suicide in persons with epilepsy, highlighting alcohol and substance abuse, living alone, seizure burden, nonadherence, and structural or unknown etiologies as key risk factors. The stronger associations for substance abuse may reflect characteristics specific to epilepsy populations and the focus on completed suicide. Screening for substance abuse and improved seizure control may contribute to suicide prevention. Major limitations include the modest number of cases and incomplete information on prior suicidal behavior.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate how three artificial intelligence (AI)-based neonatal seizure detectors (NSDs) perform in a large, clinically acquired data set and their potential to support timely seizure identification.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of continuous EEG (cEEG) recordings from 169 neonates born at ≥35 weeks gestation with neonatal encephalopathy. Seizure presence was determined by independent review by two or three pediatric encephalographers, and 2,455 individual seizures were annotated by a single expert as a pragmatic, clinically representative reference standard. Three NSDs were evaluated: a feature-based support vector machine detector (NSD1) and two deep-learning detectors (NSD2 and Persyst-15). Using an any-overlap approach, outcomes included neonate-level seizure identification, seizure-level detection, false detections per day (FD/day), and detection latency.
RESULTS: We analyzed 15,343 hours of cEEG (median 98 hours per neonate); 55 neonates (33%) had seizures. All NSDs identified ≥95% of neonates with seizures. Seizure-level detection varied: NSD2 detected 35% (IQR 17-53%), NSD1 63% (IQR 38-82%), and Persyst-15 60% (IQR 37-80%) of seizures. NSD1 generated significantly more FDs (46 FD/day, IQR 22-82) than NSD2 (3.2 IQR 1.2-9.3) and Persyst-15 (2.8 IQR 1.1-6.2; P < 0.0001). The median time to first true detection was <1 minute for NSD1 and Persyst-15, versus 26 minutes for NSD2.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based NSDs demonstrated high infant-level sensitivity but different tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and alarm burden. These findings highlight how AI tools may augment clinical EEG workflows and support earlier seizure recognition, while underscoring the need for evaluation under real-world conditions to guide safe and effective implementation.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is widely used for presurgical evaluation in epilepsy, yet practice patterns vary substantially across centers, contributing to heterogeneity in the literature. We examined differences in SEEG experience, techniques, and complications across Europe and North America centers.
METHODS: An electronic 39-item REDCap survey was distributed to centers participating in the American Stereo-EEG Consortium and EpiCARE Consortium. The survey assessed center characteristics, electrode planning and implantation, monitoring practices, and complications.
RESULTS: Sixty-six centers responded, including 38 from North America and 28 from Europe. North American centers more frequently used nurse-led ictal and postictal assessments (16/38 vs. 5/28; P = 0.06) and robotic image-guided implantation systems (37/38 vs. 17/28; P < 0.001), with a trend toward higher case volumes. Compared with European centers, North American programs were less likely to have over 15 years of SEEG experience (6/38 vs. 12/28; P = 0.015), fewer dedicated SEEG readers (12/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.001), and less frequent use of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation (13/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.01). Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequently reported among North American centers in the unadjusted analysis (9/38 vs. 1/28; p = 0.035); however, the regional difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for center SEEG experience and annual case volume.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant differences exist between North American and European SEEG practices. North American centers more commonly use robotic implantation and manage higher volume, whereas European centers demonstrate greater experience and more frequent use of SEEG-guided ablation. These findings support the need for standardized protocols to improve safety and outcomes.

papers.title: Persistent focal onchocerciasis transmission near the Maridi Dam, South Sudan, despite intensified elimination interventions: Repeated Ov16 serosurveys in young children, 2019-2026.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maridi County in South Sudan is an onchocerciasis hotspot with a high burden of onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy. Elimination activities were strengthened through slash-and-clear vector control from 2019 and biannual community-directed treatment with ivermectin from 2021. We assessed Ov16 seropositivity in young untreated children and its temporal and geographical distribution following these interventions.
METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Repeated cross-sectional Ov16 rapid diagnostic test surveys were conducted in 2019, 2023, and 2026 using the same field approach. For direct temporal comparison, analyses were restricted to children aged 3-4 years from the four sites surveyed in 2026. Overall Ov16 seroprevalence was 18.5% (36/195; 95% CI 13.4-24.8). Combined seroprevalence was 33.3% (35/105) in the two frontline villages near the Maridi Dam, Kazana 1 and Kazana 2, versus 1.1% (1/90) in the two more distant villages of Hai-Tarawa and Hai-Gabat (p < 0.001); seroprevalence reached 49.1% (26/53) in Kazana 2. Seroprevalence was 11.5% (10/87) among 3-year-olds and 24.1% (26/108) among 4-year-olds (p = 0.024). Across the same four villages and age range, overall prevalence was 14.3% (6/42) in 2019, 20.0% (14/70) in 2023, and 18.5% (36/195) in 2026 (p = 0.744). To account for unequal village representation across surveys, village-standardized prevalence estimates were also calculated by assigning equal weight to each village and closely paralleled the crude estimates. A generalized linear mixed model with village as a random intercept was fitted, adjusting for age and sex. Compared with 2019, there was no evidence of a temporal difference in seropositivity in 2023 (OR 1.32, 95% CI 0.40-4.40; p = 0.652) or 2026 (OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.43-3.60; p = 0.686).
CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Repeated Ov16 surveys identified continued substantial seropositivity among children aged 3-4 years, particularly in Kazana 2 near the Maridi Dam, consistent with recent O. volvulus exposure and ongoing local transmission. The findings support improving ivermectin coverage among eligible residents, sustained entomologically monitored vector control, and geographically targeted surveillance. Safe paediatric antifilarial options could help close the protection gap in children at risk of onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Model based Federated Learning Framework for Seizure-Type Classification.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.abstract: Accurate seizure-type identification is of great significance for epilepsy patient treatment and management. Manual electroencephalogram (EEG) data analysis, the traditional method, is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and subjective. While deep learning has shown great potential in medical diagnosis, it faces privacy and data silo challenges in handling multi-center EEG data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch model and federated learning-based automatic classification method for seizure types. A federated learning framework is introduced to facilitate multi-center data collaborative training while protecting data privacy. In the base model, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1DCNN) and the two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2DCNN) are integrated to extract the complexity features of EEG signals and the topological features of brain networks, respectively, and the dual-modal features are adaptively integrated through the dynamic attention fusion module. In local training of federated learning framework, the FedProx optimization strategy is adopted to effectively solve the model update divergence problem caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data and improve the model generalization ability. Experimental results show that the proposed federated learning framework performs well in core indicators of seizure-type classification such as accuracy and macro-average F1 score. Even in the case of extremely unbalanced data, the proposed method can still maintain an accuracy of 98.42% and a macro-average F1 score of 94.79%. This method provides an effective solution for distributed medical data collaborative training, which is of great significance for promoting the accurate diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy.
