papers.title: BiXCA-DualFormer: A time-frequency fusion model for epileptic seizure prediction.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
papers.abstract: Epileptic seizure prediction based on electroencephalography (EEG) is important for developing early-warning technologies and improving patient safety. However, reliable prediction remains challenging because preictal EEG changes are subtle and non-stationary, with discriminative information distributed across both temporal and spectral domains. The purpose of this study is to develop a seizure prediction framework that can jointly model complementary temporal and spectral EEG information and capture their interactions. To this end, we propose BiXCA-DualFormer, a dual-branch time-frequency fusion model. Raw EEG signals and short-time Fourier transform representations are processed through separate temporal and spectral branches to extract complementary waveform and frequency-domain features. The main methodological contribution of the proposed model is the introduction of bidirectional cross-attention to explicitly exchange information between the two branches, followed by a Transformer encoder and learnable query pooling for global dependency modeling and feature aggregation. Experiments on the CHB-MIT dataset showed that the proposed model achieved 95.29% accuracy, 96.40% sensitivity, 95.05% specificity, and a false positive rate of 0.0495. Ablation analysis indicated that time-frequency interaction and global contextual modeling improved sensitivity and discriminative performance. These results suggest that BiXCA-DualFormer provides an effective end-to-end biomedical signal processing framework for EEG-based seizure prediction.

papers.title: The lived experiences of caregivers of people with epilepsy in Botswana.
papers.journal: African journal of primary health care & family medicine
papers.iso_journal: Afr J Prim Health Care Fam Med
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder affecting about 50 million people worldwide. Caregivers of people with epilepsy face significant emotional, physical and psychological distress due to the demands of caregiving. Limited resources, stigma and the lack of a proper support system often worsen these challenges.
AIM: This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of caregivers of individuals with epilepsy in Botswana.
SETTING: This study was conducted in Gaborone, the capital city of Botswana, located in Botswana's South-East District.
METHODS: An interpretive phenomenological approach was used to capture the lived experiences of 13 caregivers, recruited through purposive sampling. In-depth interviews were conducted to gather qualitative data, which were analysed using the General Inductive Approach.
RESULTS: Caregivers reported significant emotional distress, including anxiety, stress and social isolation due to the unpredictable nature of seizures. Financial difficulties were dominant concern, with many caregivers losing employment status due to caregiving responsibility. High cost of medication and access to healthcare services was another burden while stigma surrounding epilepsy further exacerbated emotional strain. Additionally, caregivers reported limited coping strategies, which further contributed to their psychological distress.
CONCLUSION: The study highlights the urgent need for culturally sensitive interventions to address the psychological and economic burden faced by caregivers. Strengthening support system, ensuring reliable access to medication and providing financial aid could significantly improve caregivers' well-being and by extension, the quality of life for individuals living with epilepsy in Botswana.Contribution: This study offers important insights into caregiver experiences in epilepsy, emphasising the need for family inclusive, caregiver centred nursing practices, educational enhancement and improved community policies in Botswana. It highlights the importance of structured psychosocial support, integrating epilepsy care into home services, and culturally relevant coping strategies. These findings aim to guide targeted interventions and create more responsive health systems in similar resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Anesthetic management for coarctation of aorta repair in a very low birth weight preterm infant: a case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic management for cardiac surgery in very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants is highly challenging due to organ immaturity and metabolic vulnerability. Coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring early intervention adds further complexity. Reports on anesthesia for CoA repair in VLBW infants remain limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: A male infant born at 32⁺² weeks gestation with a VLBW of 1360 g underwent CoA repair at 39 days of age (weight 2600 g). Anesthesia was induced with etomidate (0.3 mg/kg) and maintained with sufentanil (2.5 µg/kg/h), propofol (6 mg/kg/h), and low-dose sevoflurane (0.5%). Mechanical ventilation was initiated with a tidal volume of approximately 9.6 mL/kg. Dopamine (5 µg/kg/min) was infused for hemodynamic support.
INTERVENTION: Intraoperative blood glucose was monitored at induction (4.6 mmol/L), 1 h after incision (9.8 mmol/L), and at the end of surgery (significant transient intraoperative hyperglycemia of 15.6 mmol/L). Upon detection of hyperglycemia, which was likely multifactorial and potentially related to exogenous glucose administration, surgical stress, and dopamine infusion, although definitive causality cannot be established due to the absence of endocrine or metabolic assessments, glucose-containing infusions were immediately reduced. Blood glucose normalized spontaneously within 12 h without insulin therapy.
OUTCOME: The infant remained hemodynamically stable with no seizures, hyperosmolality, or neurological complications. He was extubated on postoperative day 3, discharged on day 26, and showed good catch-up growth at one-month follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic regimens and routine, serial perioperative glucose monitoring in VLBW infants undergoing cardiac surgery. Even modest glucose infusion rates may lead to significant hyperglycemia under surgical stress, emphasizing the need for proactive glucose stewardship.

papers.title: Individualized hybrid electroconvulsive therapy (i-HECT) shows rapid anti-depressant effect in young patients with depression.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For young patients with depression, electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is highly effective but causes acute cognitive side effects. We designed a new individualized hybrid electroconvulsive therapy (i-HECT) combines ECT with low-charge electrotherapy (LCE) and individual symptom monitoring to reduce cognitive impairments.
METHODS: i-HECT comprised two treatments: ECT and LCE. ECT utilized an energy set of 1.5 times the seizure threshold (ST), while LCE was set at 0.5 ST. The initial session employed standard bilateral ECT. Subsequent sessions involved ECT or LCE, depending on whether meeting the ECT-LCE transition criteria (Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score < 22 or ≥ 50% reduction), assessed after each session. This trial employed a Simon's optimal two-stage design with a 3-month follow-up period in 46 young patients (age 16-25) with depression (MADRS ≥ 22).
RESULTS: The intention-to-treat analysis revealed an 80.4% response rate and a 58.7% remission rate, The reduction in MADRS score was 19.1 ± 7.0, with Hedges' g = 3.29 (95% CI = 2.66 to 3.91). The orientation recovery tests (ORTs) took 22.7 ± 11.3 min after LCEs and 26.0 ± 10.3 min after ECTs. Improvements in cognitive functions were observed after i-HECT treatments and during the 3-month follow-up periods.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our i-HECT protocol shows promise as a simple and rapid treatment option for young patients with depression, with observed improvements in cognitive function.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (http://www.chictr.org.cn), registration number: ChiCTR2100045682. Date of registration on April 23, 2021.

papers.title: [The novelties of adult advanced life support and post-resuscitation therapy according to the 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines].
papers.abstract: The European Resuscitation Council published its updated Guidelines for Resuscitation in 2025. The revised guidelines highlight advanced life support and post-resuscitation care, as well as post-resuscitation rehabilitation, as the third and fourth links in the updated Chain of Survival. In this review, we summarize the key updates and principal messages of the new guideline on advanced life support and post-resuscitation care. Although the Advanced Life Support guidelines do not represent a paradigm shift, they place a stronger emphasis on delivering high-quality, timely resuscitation. High-quality chest compressions remain the cornerstone of resuscitation, complemented by early, safe, and correctly performed defibrillation with minimal interruptions, appropriate drug administration, and prompt identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The updated guidelines also address emerging topics, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation-induced consciousness, the specific considerations for cardiac arrest occurring in closely monitored patients, and the introduction of physiology-guided resuscitation. Similarly, the post-resuscitation care guidelines introduce no major changes compared with previous recommendations. Instead, they reinforce the importance of delivering high-quality post-resuscitation care, with particular emphasis on neuroprotection. The key components of the stabilization, diagnostic, and optimization phases include an ABCDE approach to patient assessment, optimization of oxygenation, ventilation, and hemodynamic status, seizure management, prevention of fever during the first 72 hours after return of spontaneous circulation, and identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The indications for immediate coronary angiography following successful cardiopulmonary resuscitation have been further refined, and the guidelines also clarify the diagnostic approach when a non-cardiac cause of cardiac arrest is suspected. Greater emphasis is placed on multimodal neuroprognosis and post-resuscitation rehabilitation. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1810-1824.

papers.title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
papers.abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up. In patients with severe pregnancy-induced hypertension, PRES warrants recognition as a potential complication; management should prioritize rigorous blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, alleviation of pregnancy-related physiological stress, and timely neuroimaging to guide treatment, with strategies balancing maternal and fetal safety-early recognition and intervention underpinned by standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration being critical to improving prognosis and reducing complications.

papers.title: A Human iPSC-Derived Neuron and Glioma Culture Model Reveals Increased Neuronal Excitability and Loss of GABAergic Inhibition.
papers.abstract: Gliomas engage in bidirectional interactions with neural circuits, driving hyperexcitability, disruption of excitatory-inhibitory balance, and tumor-associated seizures. Human in vitro models that enable functional interrogation of tumor-induced changes in glutamatergic-GABAergic neuronal crosstalk remain limited. We established a defined human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived culture comprising of glutamatergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, and astrocytes with and without glioma cells. Network maturation and function were characterized using immunocytochemistry, multi-electrode array recordings, and whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology. Neuronal cultures developed mature synaptic architecture, spontaneous coordinated network activity, and suppression of neuronal firing following treatment with the GABA-A agonist muscimol, demonstrating functional GABAergic signaling. Glioma incorporation increased spike rate, increased coordinated network activity, and reversed the response to muscimol from suppression to elevation of neuronal firing, indicating disrupted GABAergic signaling. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings demonstrated increased intrinsic excitability of glutamatergic neurons following glioma co-culture, characterized by increased action potential firing frequency and increased action potential amplitude. This human iPSC-derived glutamatergic-GABAergic neuron model recapitulates key features of tumor-induced neuronal dysfunction while enabling complementary network- and single-cell analyses. The model provides a relevant, scalable, and accessible system for mechanistic investigation of bidirectional neuron-glioma interactions and preclinical evaluation of therapies targeting tumor-induced neuronal dysfunction.

papers.title: Intraoperative Very High-Frequency Activity for Localization of the Epileptogenic Zone: An International Multicenter Study.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Interictal spikes on intraoperative electrocorticography have been used to localize the epileptogenic zone but have limited specificity. We hypothesized that identifying spatially distributed, spike-associated very high-frequency activity (vHFA; 500-2,000 Hz) would improve the ability of spikes to localize the epileptogenic zone. We aimed to characterize spike-associated vHFA and to determine whether a seizure outcome prediction model incorporating vHFA could be externally validated across independent centers.
METHODS: This retrospective two-center cohort study included patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy who underwent electrocorticography and subsequent resection between January 2016 and May 2025. Spikes occurring across contacts within 50 ms were classified as co-occurring; all others were classified as isolated. We determined whether vHFA was associated with co-occurring spikes. We then assessed whether contacts enriched in vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes were more likely to be located within the resected region among seizure-free patients. Finally, we determined whether the rate of such spikes remaining outside the resection predicted seizure outcomes across the two centers.
RESULTS: Among 56 patients (mean age: 21.2 years; 26 females), we identified 132,359 spikes, of which 1,925 were vHFA-positive. The vHFA peak preceded the associated spike peak by 8.0 ms (95%CI: 5.0-16.0). vHFA-positive spikes were more likely to be classified as co-occurring, even after adjustment for anatomy and inter-electrode distance (OR: 3.43; 95%CI: 2.82-4.17). Among the 35 seizure-free patients, contacts with higher rates of vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes were more likely to be resected (OR: 11.92 per occurrence/min; 95%CI: 5.62-25.32). This association was stronger than that observed for all spikes (OR: 1.09 per occurrence/min; 95%CI: 1.06-1.11). Twenty patients experienced postoperative seizure recurrence; a higher proportion of vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes in preserved areas was associated with recurrence (OR: 3.22 per 0.01 increase in proportion; 95%CI: 1.14-9.12). In bidirectional cross-center validation, models incorporating vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.80 and 0.69, with better performance when the model was developed using the larger sample.
DISCUSSION: Spike-associated vHFA may identify a biologically meaningful subset of interictal spikes involved in propagation across the epileptogenic zone. vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes may represent a generalizable intraoperative biomarker of the epileptogenic zone.

papers.title: The role of the NLRP3 inflammasome in a CLN2 mouse model of neuroinflammation.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses, or Batten disease, comprises a group of inherited pediatric neurodegenerative disorders, and is characterized by the lysosomal accumulation of the fluorescent storage material lipofuscin. The human classical late-infantile form of the disorder (CLN2) is caused by mutations in the CLN2 / Tripeptidyl peptidase 1 ( TPP1 ) gene. Comparable to human CLN2, a knockout of the Tpp1 gene ( Tpp1 -/- ) in the mouse leads to progressive vision loss, ataxia, motor atrophy, seizures, and premature death. While we previously showed using bulk RNA-seq analysis that reactive gliosis develops between 3 and 4 months in this animal model, the role of the inflammasome in CLN2 remains unexplored. The inflammasome is a multiprotein complex formed through pattern recognition receptor engagement, which culminate in the cleavage and release of interleukin-1 beta. Here we report that while some inflammasome-associated genes are upregulated as early as 1-month in the Tpp1 -/- cerebellum, it is not until 3-months-old that all gene transcripts necessary for inflammasome assembly and function are upregulated, leading to IL1β release. In Tpp1 -/- slice cultures, we demonstrated that MCC950, an inhibitor of inflammasome assembly, downregulates transcriptional expression of genes associated with reactive microglia and inflammasome function. Furthermore, prophylactic administration of MCC950 in drinking water of Tpp1 -/- animals for two months is sufficient to lower the expression of these same genes in the forebrain and cerebellum, suggesting that inflammasome inhibitors are promising therapeutics for CLN2 and neurodegeneration broadly.

papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: Many studies using mouse models of human brain disorders rely on extended recordings of brain electrical activity through electroencephalogram, or EEG. The features that researchers measure in these recordings, such as seizures and epileptiform activity, are deeply influenced by whether the animal is awake, in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, or in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Because total sleep duration varies naturally across animals, rigorous experimental comparisons require classifying the sleep state of every few seconds of a recording. Manual annotation is highly labor-intensive, often requiring hours per subject. While automated scoring tools accelerate this process, they are typically trained exclusively on healthy cohorts and frequently fail when applied to disease models that exhibit atypical or fragmented sleep architecture. Somnus is an open-source Python package designed to automate rodent sleep staging using EEG, muscle activity (EMG), and optional video-tracking data. It includes a robust base model trained on diverse recordings from six independent laboratories, enabling out-of-the-box classification across various equipment setups without requiring prior manual labeling. A central feature of Somnus is its capacity for rapid adaptation to pathological sleep structure. The software provides a graphical interface that directs researchers to the specific epochs where the base model is least certain. Users can manually correct these targeted epochs in a built-in viewer by comparing the model's classification to the raw EEG signal and video, and then use their corrections to fine-tune the model. This workflow empowers researchers to generate accurate custom scorers for complex disease models or novel treatments with just a few minutes of manual correction, bypassing the need to hand-score entire experimental cohorts or develop their own models from scratch.

papers.title: GAT1508, a selective neuronal GIRK1/2 activator, exhibits superior antiepileptic efficacy and synergizes with cannabidiol.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK; Kir3) channels are key regulators of neuronal excitability and represent promising therapeutic targets for epilepsy. Here, we characterize GAT1508, a urea-based small-molecule activator selectively targeting neuronal GIRK1/2 heterotetramers, and compare its efficacy with previously described urea compounds ML297 and GiGA1. In a pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced seizure model, GAT1508 demonstrated robust antiseizure activity, outperforming both ML297 and GiGA1 and achieving efficacy comparable to valproic acid. Electrophysiological studies using two-electrode voltage clamp in Xenopus oocytes revealed that GAT1508, unlike ML297 and GiGA1, selectively activates GIRK1/2 channels without significant activation of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels, suggesting reduced risk of cardiovascular side effects. Structural and computational analyses indicate that enhanced stabilization of GAT1508 compared to ML297 within the GIRK1/2 binding pocket promotes both ion permeation and channel gating through coordinated interactions with key residues. Furthermore, GAT1508, like the two other urea drugs, exhibited synergistic activation of GIRK channels when combined with Gβγ-mediated pathways and significantly potentiated the antiseizure effects of cannabidiol (CBD) in both hippocampal slice recordings and in vivo seizure models. These findings establish GAT1508 as a potent and selective GIRK1/2 activator and support a novel combination therapeutic strategy for epilepsy based on convergent GIRK channel modulation.

papers.title: Drug consumption pattern of drivers causing traffic accidents with a motor vehicle in Hungary (2014-2023).
papers.abstract: Driving under the influence of drugs (DUID) is a recognized risk factor for traffic accidents, but data on accident-involved drivers in Hungary are scarce. We characterized drug use among 1563 drivers classified by the police as at fault for a traffic accident and tested on suspicion of drug use (DCA) between 2014 and 2023, and compared their toxicological profile with a previously reported cohort of drivers suspected of DUID at roadside checks (sDUID) from the same region and period. Blood and urine samples were screened for illicit drugs, psychoactive medicines and new psychoactive substances by gas and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Temporal trends were assessed using annual proportions of tested drivers and negative binomial regression with the annual number of tested drivers as an offset. Differences in the distribution of substance categories between DCA and sDUID drivers were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test, followed by post-hoc binomial tests with Bonferroni correction. Overall, 1308 drivers (83.7%) tested positive: classical illicit drugs in 48.6%, psychoactive medicines in 44.2%, synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists (SCRA) in 15.4% and stimulant new psychoactive substances (sNPS) in 9.94%. Benzodiazepines accounted for 84.1% of medicine-positive cases and exceeded the upper therapeutic limit in 55.6% of these. Benzodiazepines and SCRA were more frequent among DCA than sDUID drivers, whereas active tetrahydrocannabinol was more frequent among sDUID drivers. National seizure trends broadly mirrored these prevalence. Because both cohorts were selected by police suspicion, these differences express relative enrichment rather than accident risk. They nevertheless indicate that benzodiazepine-related impairment is less conspicuous at roadside checks and may be systematically under-detected.

papers.title: Variables associated with epilepsy self-management competency among people with epilepsy from an epilepsy self-management clinical trial.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Epilepsy is a chronic illness that requires ongoing self-management. Our study aimed to identify clinical and demographic variables associated with self-management competency as measured by the epilepsy self-management scale (ESMS). We hypothesized that female gender, higher level of education, and higher income were independently correlated with greater self-management competency.
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis of baseline data in PWE (N = 160) experiencing negative health events enrolled in the 6-month clinical trial SMART examined categories of self-management including seizure, lifestyle, medication, safety, and information management. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), regression was used for variable selection. To exclude false positives, the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was employed, to control the False discovery rate (FDR) q-values < 0.05.
RESULTS: Variables correlated with greater total self-management competency were having a seizure within the past 30 days (p = 0.008), greater self-efficacy (p < 0.001), lower comorbidity (p = 0.008), and lower functional status (p < 0.001). Higher self-efficacy was associated with improved self-management competency across each self-management subdomain.
CONCLUSION: Our analysis found that self-efficacy was associated with total self-management competency as well as competency in lifestyle, medication, information, safety, and seizure management. Future research may focus on methods to increase self-efficacy.

papers.title: Early recurrence of febrile seizures in the pediatric emergency department: development and internal validation of FSERS, a practical bedside risk score.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Febrile seizures (FS) are common and generally benign. Early recurrence within 24 h does not itself mandate admission or treatment but may prompt reassessment before discharge, particularly when atypical or evolving features raise concern for an alternative acute neurologic diagnosis. We aimed to develop and internally validate a bedside score for early FS recurrence.
METHODS: We included 400 children with confirmed FS presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department (PED) between January 2020 and December 2024. Complex-phenotype FS was defined by focal onset or prolonged duration only. Backward stepwise multivariable logistic regression derived a parsimonious model, followed by 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation.
RESULTS: Early recurrence occurred in 45/400 children (11.2%). Independent predictors were neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.345), seizure duration (aOR 1.154), C-reactive protein (CRP; aOR 1.187), serum sodium (aOR 0.606), and fever-to-seizure interval (aOR 0.821). The continuous model achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.924 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.897. The derived integer FS Early Recurrence Score (FSERS) had an apparent AUC of 0.905 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.887.
CONCLUSIONS: FSERS integrates five readily available variables into an internally validated estimate of early FS recurrence risk. It is not an admission rule, treatment trigger, or diagnostic model for central nervous system infection or acute encephalopathy, and should complement clinical reassessment and red-flag evaluation. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before score-based changes in observation or disposition are considered.

papers.title: Abnormal SEP recovery amongst multimodal electrophysiological studies to indicate cortical dysfunction in PME.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progressive myoclonic epilepsies (PMEs) are rare neurodegenerative disorders characterized by cortical hyperexcitability and progressive neurological deterioration. We aimed to identify electrophysiological markers of cortical dysfunction using multimodal neurophysiological assessment.
METHODS: Seventeen adult PME patients underwent clinical evaluation and video-EEG recording. Somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP), SEP recovery function and surround inhibition, blink reflex, and motor evoked potentials (MEP) were assessed in 11 patients and compared with 11 matched healthy controls.
RESULTS: Generalized epileptiform discharges were observed in all patients. SEP recordings demonstrated increased N20/P25 amplitudes and prolonged P14, N18, and P25 latencies. SEP recovery showed marked attenuation at the shortest interstimulus interval followed by rapid amplitude recovery. Surround inhibition was preserved. Blink reflex studies revealed prolonged R2 latencies and increased amplitudes. MEP parameters did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: PME is associated with abnormal SEP recovery dynamics and giant SEPs, consistent with impaired somatosensory inhibitory processing. Blink reflex abnormalities suggest additional subcortical involvement, whereas corticospinal excitability appears relatively preserved.

papers.title: Anesthetic Care of Children With Epilepsy Receiving Ketogenic Diet Therapy: An Educational Review.
papers.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ketogenic diet therapy (KDT) is a nonpharmacologic treatment for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy that induces ketosis through high-fat, low-carbohydrate intake. These children frequently present for anesthesia, and their baseline metabolic alterations, compounded by fasting and surgical stress, place them at higher risk of perioperative complications than other pediatric patients. This educational review organizes anesthetic considerations into preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases and synthesizes them into best-practice recommendations for perianesthesia clinicians.
DESIGN: Educational review.
METHODS: A research librarian-assisted search of PubMed and Ovid MEDLINE was conducted in June 2025, limited to English-language publications from 2015 forward; of 202 unique records screened, 83 underwent full-text review, and 14 met inclusion criteria, and an unrestricted hand-search of included studies' reference lists added seven more, for 21 included studies (seven case reports, one case series, five retrospective record reviews, two prospective cohorts, two animal studies, three narrative reviews, and one summary of expert opinion).
FINDINGS: Across this literature, the central requirement is maintenance of ketosis throughout all phases of perioperative care, with evaluation of every medication and intravenous fluid for carbohydrate and gluconeogenic potential, metabolic monitoring with prompt recognition and treatment of acidosis and hypoglycemia, anesthetic technique tailored to the patient's comorbidities and the planned procedure, and interdisciplinary coordination with the ketogenic diet team.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base remains dominated by case reports and retrospective record reviews, with no randomized trials in this population, limiting generalizability; nonetheless, reviews and guidelines published since 2020 provide a workable foundation for safe perioperative care.

papers.title: Roseola infantum and subsequent epilepsy: A nationwide 20-year retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study was undertaken to evaluate whether roseola infantum is associated with an increased risk of subsequent epilepsy.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database from January 2002 to December 2021. Children with roseola, identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) code B08.2, were matched 1:1 by age and sex with children without roseola. Participants were followed from the date of roseola diagnosis, or the corresponding index date for controls, until incident epilepsy, death, or the end of the study period. The primary epilepsy definition required at least two medical encounters with ICD-10 code G40.x listed among the top five discharge diagnoses and cumulative antiseizure medication prescriptions for 180 days or longer. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with adjustment for prespecified baseline and time-varying covariates. Sensitivity analyses used a more inclusive epilepsy definition.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1 595 494 children: 797 747 with roseola and 797 747 matched controls. The mean age at cohort entry was 1.15 years, and 51.0% were male. During a mean follow-up of 10.5 years, roseola was associated with an increased risk of subsequent epilepsy (adjusted HR = 2.00, 95% CI = 1.91-2.09). The association was consistent across prespecified subgroups, with adjusted HRs ranging from 1.66 to 3.60. Postindex febrile convulsion showed the strongest independent association with epilepsy (adjusted HR = 12.31, 95% CI = 11.82-12.83). In sensitivity analyses using the inclusive epilepsy definition, roseola remained associated with increased epilepsy risk (adjusted HR = 1.52, 95% CI = 1.48-1.57).
SIGNIFICANCE: In this nationwide cohort study, roseola infantum was associated with an increased risk of subsequent epilepsy. These findings demonstrate a population-level association between roseola infantum and epilepsy and warrant prospective studies with virologic confirmation and detailed epilepsy phenotyping.

papers.title: Seizure quantification using wearable devices.
papers.abstract: Accurate assessment of seizure occurrence is central to treatment optimization, risk stratification, and management of epilepsy, yet remains largely dependent on patient-reported seizure diaries, which are frequently incomplete and unreliable. Wearable technologies have emerged as promising tools to enable objective and continuous seizure monitoring by capturing seizure-induced physiological signals. Over the past decade, substantial progress has been made in the development and clinical validation of wearable seizure detection systems, particularly for generalized convulsive seizures, where high sensitivity can be achieved, whereas detection of nonconvulsive seizures remains more limited. However, translating detection into clinically meaningful seizure quantification presents important challenges, including variability in performance across seizure types, patient populations, and individual physiological responses, as well as differences between controlled and real-world settings. This narrative review critically examines wearable technologies for seizure quantification, integrating recent clinical evidence and expert perspectives. We discuss key sensor modalities, including accelerometry, electrocardiography-derived features such as heart rate variability, multimodal biosignal integration, and emerging ultra-long-term wearable and subcutaneous electroencephalographic systems. Each modality offers specific advantages and limitations depending on seizure type and clinical context. Attention is also given to the importance of user trust, adherence, and data quality as key determinants of clinical utility. We further examine the role of wearable seizure quantification in clinical practice, including treatment monitoring, tele-epileptology, and clinical trials, as well as potential future contributions to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy risk assessment. With continued technological advances and robust real-world clinical validation, wearable systems have the potential to transform seizure monitoring and support more precise, data-driven epilepsy care.

papers.title: Two-stage spatiotemporal graph neural network framework for seizure onset zone localization.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurate localization of the seizure onset zone (SOZ) is critical for the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy. Intracranial electroencephalography captures high-resolution seizure dynamics, but interpreting complex spatiotemporal patterns across implanted electrodes is clinically challenging. We propose a two-stage, uncertainty-aware framework for SOZ localization that integrates patient-specific seizure modeling with cross-patient probabilistic ranking to estimate the likelihood of each electrode belonging to the SOZ.
METHODS: The framework was evaluated on a bi-institutional cohort of 36 patients (20 with good surgical outcome, 16 with poor surgical outcome), comprising 184 seizures. In the first stage, a patient-specific spatiotemporal graph neural network modeled seizure onset as a network-level transition using directed functional connectivity graphs derived from burst-integrated electrophysiological features. Trained solely to detect preictal-to-ictal transitions, this model generated electrode probability trajectories without SOZ supervision. In the second stage, these trajectories were summarized into interpretable descriptors and used to train a patient-agnostic classifier assigning SOZ likelihood scores to electrodes. Evaluation and hyperparameter optimization were performed using nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation restricted to good outcome patients, ensuring strict patient-level separation between training, validation, and test data.
RESULTS: Seizure onset detection was stable across patients, with comparable binary cross-entropy values between outcome groups (median = .495 vs. .438, p = .108). In good outcome patients, SOZ electrodes were prioritized among top-ranked contacts (area under the curve = .86 ± .06), with all patients exhibiting at least one SOZ electrode within the top positions. In poor outcome patients, predictions exhibited reduced spatial separability, lower likelihood magnitudes, and near-zero confidence gaps, reflecting attenuated model confidence.
SIGNIFICANCE: This two-stage framework integrates spatial interactions, temporal dynamics, and probabilistic ranking within a pipeline. By providing graded SOZ likelihood estimates and uncertainty-aware prioritization, the approach is a decision-support tool to assist hypothesis refinement during presurgical evaluation rather than as a standalone diagnostic system.

papers.title: Spatial correspondence between spontaneous brain activity alterations and normative molecular and neurochemical architecture in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric epilepsy is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed brain networks, but the molecular context of spontaneous brain activity alterations remains incompletely understood. This study investigated regional spontaneous brain activity alterations in pediatric epilepsy and their spatial correspondence with normative molecular reference maps.
METHODS: In this observational case-control neuroimaging study, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data from 44 children with epilepsy and 44 healthy controls selected using group-level frequency matching for age and sex were analyzed. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional ALFF (fALFF) were compared between groups. The unthresholded signed ALFF case-control t-map was subsequently parcellated using the Schaefer 2018 400-parcel atlas. The 200 left-hemisphere cortical parcels were spatially related to normative adult Allen Human Brain Atlas gene-expression data using partial least squares (PLS) regression, and the whole-cortex ALFF map was compared with 39 normative adult neurotransmitter maps.
RESULTS: First partial least squares component (PLS1) explained 36.42% of the variance in the left-hemisphere cortical ALFF map and was significant under 10,000 spherical spin permutations (P_spin=0.0004); regional PLS1 scores were positively associated with ALFF t-values (ρ=0.5650, P_spin=0.0004). PLS1-associated genes were enriched for synaptic, ion-transport, membrane-regulation, and neuronal-projection annotations, and inhibitory-neuron gene sets showed significant enrichment (P=0.0014). The signed ALFF map showed inverse spatial associations with the MU_CARFENTANIL_c11 μ-opioid receptor map (median Spearman ρ=-0.3317, mean Fisher z=-0.3448, P_spin=0.0003, q_FDR =0.0044) and the mGluR5_abp_hc73_smart map (median Spearman ρ=-0.2610, mean Fisher z=-0.2672, P_spin=0.0001, q_FDR =0.0022).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide indirect atlas-based spatial molecular context for the pediatric imaging phenotype. Because the molecular maps were derived from independent adult reference datasets, the associations should not be interpreted as patient-specific gene-expression or receptor measurements, causal mechanisms, or developmentally matched molecular abnormalities.

papers.title: Joubert syndrome with hippocampal malrotation in a 4-month-old male: A case report.
papers.abstract: Joubert syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive ciliopathy characterized by a distinctive midbrain-hindbrain malformation, with the "molar tooth sign" as its characteristic neuroimaging hallmark, resulting from cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, thickening and horizontalization of the superior cerebellar peduncles, and a deepened interpeduncular fossa. We report a 4-month-old male infant presenting with developmental delay and progressive weight loss. Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging revealed the characteristic molar tooth sign, vermian hypoplasia, and an associated hippocampal malrotation, a less frequently recognized but increasingly documented supratentorial finding in Joubert syndrome and related disorders. The patient also had retinal degeneration and elevated transaminases, findings that raise concern for multisystem involvement within the Joubert ciliopathy spectrum. Hippocampal malrotation has been described as an associated supratentorial finding in JS, but its clinical significance, including any relationship with epilepsy, remains uncertain. This case emphasizes careful evaluation of both infratentorial and supratentorial structures and systemic assessment in patients with JS.

papers.title: Effectiveness, safety and therapeutic potential of medical cannabis across treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical cannabis has been suggested to have a therapeutic role in selected treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. We analyzed the available evidence to assess the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders.
METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, EBSCO, and PubMed for studies published between January 1, 1970, and April 25, 2026. We considered studies examining any type or formulation of medical cannabis in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Primary outcomes were disorder-specific clinical improvement measures. Safety outcomes were adverse events, serious adverse events, and withdrawals due to adverse events. Evidence from studies was synthesized as equivalent odds ratios (eORs) for comparative outcomes and as pooled proportions for single-arm safety outcomes, via random-effects meta-analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, and structured quality assessment for case series and case reports, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251148868.
FINDINGS: 127 eligible studies were included, of which 32 studies involving 3645 participants contributed to meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed improvement in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.72), refractory pain (eOR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.30-0.78), and refractory multiple sclerosis spasticity (eOR = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.07-0.75). Evidence for psychiatric disorders was scarce. Small randomized trials reported improvement in PTSD-related nightmares and cannabis dependence after failed cessation. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in hyperarousal, residual obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and refractory Tourette syndrome. Findings for treatment-resistant anxiety were inconsistent, and schizophrenia did not show a reliable therapeutic effect. Controlled analyses showed higher odds of any adverse events in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.52-3.23) and refractory multiple sclerosis (eOR = 1.89, 95% CI = 1.01-3.52), with higher odds of serious adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events also observed in drug-resistant epilepsy. In single-arm and real-world studies, pooled proportions of any adverse events ranged from 15.5% in multiple sclerosis to 66.0% in Tourette syndrome, with substantial heterogeneity.
INTERPRETATION: Adjunctive pharmaceutical cannabidiol has the most consistent comparative evidence for reducing seizure frequency in selected drug-resistant epilepsy. Evidence for refractory pain and multiple sclerosis is heterogeneous and varies by clinical indication, cannabinoid formulation, and outcome definition. Evidence in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders remains limited and is insufficient to support routine clinical recommendations. Further high-quality studies directly examining diagnosis-specific and formulation-specific effects, safety, and tolerability are needed.

papers.title: Self-Guided Beta-Responsive Visual Neurofeedback in a Public Exhibition: Feasibility and Usability Randomized Controlled rial.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurofeedback is studied for stress and anxiety regulation, but most systems require supervision or research-grade equipment. Consumer electroencephalography (EEG) could broaden access, yet autonomous first-contact feasibility, usability, and baseline neural-state effects remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: We assessed autonomous completion and usability, tested whether a fixed breathing pacer improved outcomes over visual neurofeedback alone, and explored whether pretask resting beta was associated with usability.
METHODS: We conducted a single-session, 2-arm randomized feasibility and usability trial at a public science exhibition in Bern, Switzerland, between March and June 2025. Eligible adults were aged 18 years or older, could read German or French, and reported no epilepsy or implanted electronic device. A tablet app guided participants without experimenter assistance through consent, setup, a 30-second eyes-closed baseline, 1:1 randomization, a 120-second beta-responsive task, and questionnaires. The final analytic sample included participants assigned to visual neurofeedback only (VN; n=27) or visual neurofeedback plus a 6 breaths/minute breathing pacer (VN+BP; n=25). Outcomes were usability, relaxation, and state mindfulness. Data were collected prospectively; no secondary data were used. Analyses used Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, Spearman, and permutation tests (2-sided, α=.05); EEG outcome and item analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: Of 110 visitors initiating a session, 79 completed the task with a valid EEG recording (71.8%, 95% CI 62.8-79.4) and 52 met analytic criteria (47.3%, 95% CI 38.2%-56.5%). Participants (35 women) had a mean age of 39.0 (SD 11.3) years. Usability was good (System Usability Scale [SUS] mean 72.3, SD 14.7; 95% CI 68.3-76.2), and 31/52 participants scored at least 68 (59.6%, 95% CI 46.1%-71.8%). Usability did not differ between VN and VN+BP (median 75.0, IQR 62.5-81.3 vs median 72.5, IQR 65.0-90.0; Mann-Whitney U=362.5, P=.65; rank-biserial r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.25). Relaxation (median 63.0, IQR 50.0-80.0 vs median 61.0, IQR 50.0-67.0; Mann-Whitney U=276.5, P=.27; r=0.18, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.49) and mindfulness (median 2.4, IQR 2.1-2.8 vs median 2.5, IQR 2.0-3.2; Mann-Whitney U=346.5, P=.68; r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.26) did not differ. Higher resting beta was associated with lower SUS before correction (Spearman ρ=-0.31, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.04; raw P=.03), but not after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted P=.30). SUS item analyses showed a global pattern (permutation P=.02), strongest for functional integration (ρ=-0.43, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.18; Holm-adjusted P=.01).
CONCLUSIONS: This trial evaluated an autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback system integrating self-fitting, signal-quality checking, baseline calibration, adaptive feedback, randomization, and self-report without operator support. Many first-time users completed the autonomous workflow with acceptable-to-good usability; a fixed, open-loop breathing pacer did not improve usability, relaxation, or state mindfulness; and higher resting beta showed a preliminary association with lower perceived usability. These findings support autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback and motivate work on adaptive onboarding, validated EEG pipelines, and objective self-regulation outcomes.

papers.title: Attitudes toward treating functional neurological disorders: psychological service provider perspectives.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Functional neurological disorders (FND) are characterized by involuntary sensory, motor, and/or other seemingly neurological symptoms lacking expected medical explanation. Once diagnosed, patients often are referred to mental health providers for psychotherapy, which is effective in treating many FND symptom presentations either alone or as part of an integrative approach. Mental health providers may feel reluctant or unprepared to accept these referrals, however.
METHODS: We conducted a U.S.-based online survey of 286 practicing psychological service providers (psychologists, psychiatrists, counselors, social workers in private practice, neuropsychologists) to examine knowledge of, attitudes toward, and preparedness to treat FND.
RESULTS: Findings revealed that most of our sample had limited exposure to FND in routine practice. Confidence in treating FND was modest, with neuropsychologists reporting more knowledge of and more confidence in treating FND than other psychologists/mental health providers. Greater perceived adequacy of psychotherapy training for, and more experience working with, FND each were associated with more positive FND attitudes, including greater confidence and enjoyment in treating FND and greater belief that symptoms would improve.
DISCUSSION: This study is novel in its examination of knowledge and attitudes among psychological service providers, who are pivotal in furnishing effective treatment for FND patients but may not be well-versed in their needs. In contrast to existing studies of medical providers that revealed stigma as a major barrier to providing adequate care for FND, our findings suggest lack of knowledge and lack of access to FND patients may limit the ability to gain more training and expertise. Targeted training and consultation for mental health providers may improve confidence and motivation and expand the workforce capable of delivering effective treatment for FND.

papers.title: Comprehensive 3-Year Pediatric Resident Resuscitation Simulation Curriculum on the Care of the Severely Ill Pediatric Patient.
papers.journal: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric residents must be able to manage severely ill patients by the end of training. Simulation provides training in low-frequency, high-risk clinical situations. A longitudinal simulation curriculum could provide consistent training for residents to develop these essential skills.
METHODS: We utilized Kern's 6 steps of curriculum development. A needs assessment identified content gaps. We implemented a 3-year, 9-case resuscitation simulation curriculum for pediatric residents targeting shock (septic, hypovolemic, obstructive), arrhythmias (supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, asystole), and respiratory failure (with bradycardia, seizures, hypoventilation). Each year, participants completed 3 simulation cases over 3 hours utilizing high-technology manikins. Patients ranged from 10 days to 10 years. We assessed the curriculum using Kirkpatrick's model, including reaction data assessing for change in self-reported confidence recognizing and managing targeted clinical events from pre/postsurveys, free-text responses noting areas of improved knowledge on postsurveys, and chart review of code events assessing for behavior change if residents led actual codes.
RESULTS: Ninety-two pediatric residents completed the curriculum. Participation was associated with improved confidence recognizing and managing targeted clinical events (pre: median 3-4, interquartile range [IQR] 3-5; post: 4-5, IQR 4-5; P < .05). Themes of lessons learned included increased knowledge in clinical management, crisis resource management skills, and local resources. Residents were more likely to assume the code leader role in actual patient codes postcurriculum (10% pre vs 40% post).
DISCUSSION: Participation in the curriculum was associated with increased resident confidence recognizing and managing targeted content, improved knowledge, and greater resident participation as code leaders in actual codes.

papers.title: Bilateral, Asynchronous, Inferior Shoulder Dislocation in a Multidisabled Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inferior glenohumeral dislocation, or luxatio erecta humeri (LEH), is an exceptionally rare injury accounting for approximately 0.5% of all shoulder dislocations. It typically results from high-energy trauma through hyperabduction or direct axial loading, forcing the humeral head inferiorly and locking the arm in abduction. While unilateral presentation is rare, bilateral occurrence is extraordinary. Diagnostic or therapeutic delays can cause severe, permanent neurovascular and musculoskeletal sequelae.
CASE REPORT: A 42-year-old male with profound neurodevelopmental disabilities - including cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, total blindness, and epilepsy - residing in a long-term care facility presented with an acute right LEH. Attempted closed reduction at an orthopedic center was unsuccessful, and the patient was discharged against medical advice without definitive intervention. Four years later, at age 46, the patient presented with a neglected, chronic left LEH. Due to the chronic, fixed nature of the bilateral injuries, the dislocations were deemed un-reducible, resulting in a profound and permanent accumulation of orthopedic disability.
CONCLUSION: Managing LEH in patients with severe developmental disabilities presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Cognitive and communication barriers often cause diagnostic overshadowing, leading to missed or severely delayed presentations. Furthermore, management is frequently complicated by patient uncooperativeness, high-risk anesthesia profiles, and increased risks of operative failure.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-generated and algorithmically personalized music interventions and their effects on brain function, behavior, and health: a critical review.
papers.abstract: This critical review synthesizes empirical studies of algorithmically personalized and artificial-intelligence-generated music interventions reporting neurophysiological, neuroimaging, or objective behavioral outcomes. Literature was identified through structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library through 12 August 2026, with CNKI and Wanfang searched on 22 September 2026, supplemented by citation tracking. Twenty-one eligible studies (at least 1,005 participants) were identified. Five things the term artificial intelligence covers in this literature are separated: algorithmic selection from a corpus, rule-based sonification, parametric modulation of pre-existing material, machine-learning generative composition, and closed-loop delivery contingent on the listener's own signal. Only three studies used a machine-learning generative model, so most of the evidence concerns algorithmic personalization of existing material. Studies of closed-loop neural systems reported the most consistent neurophysiological signal, and music-based alpha neurofeedback produced higher normalized alpha power than yoked random feedback. In an open-loop design, personalized EEG-derived music was reported to attenuate anxiety induction where self-selected preferred music and silence did not, with enhanced prefrontal theta oscillations as the associated correlate. Eight studies carried a comparator capable of isolating an algorithmic component from music exposure, and all eight favored the algorithmic condition. These eight address different causal questions, use different designs, and point to no single mechanism, so their results are best read as preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Evidence quality was very low throughout. The median reported sample size was 22, no study blinded participants or measured expectancy, and no specific finding has been independently replicated. GRADE certainty was very low for every outcome domain, covering EEG oscillatory power, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, epileptiform activity, and cognitive, behavioral and affective outcomes. Neurophysiological change is reported more often than behavioral change, and behavioral change more often than clinical benefit. The evidence supports continued investigation and does not support clinical deployment. Eight reporting and design requirements for future trials are proposed.

papers.title: Cognitive Test Performance in CLN3 Disease Is Associated With the CLN3 Staging System (CLN3SS).
papers.abstract: CLN3 disease is an inherited neurodegenerative disease, typically with childhood onset, and characterized by vision loss, seizures, cognitive decline, and difficulties. The CLN3 Staging System (CLN3SS) characterizes disease progression. Our aim was to assess differences in cognitive test scores in relation to CLN3SS among individuals with CLN3 disease. We evaluated the relationship between cognitive test performance and the CLN3SS in individuals with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease. Participants completed tasks of verbal reasoning, vocabulary knowledge, attention, fund of information, and ability to recite the alphabet. One-way ANOVA testing assessed differences in mean cognitive test score among CLN3SS score groups, and chi-square testing was used to compare the proportion in each CLN3SS group that could recite the alphabet. Data were evaluated from a sample of 85 individuals with a total 245 CLN3SS assessments conducted within 6 months of their cognitive testing, A significant decrease in test scores was found between CLN3SS Stages 1 (vision loss present) and 2 (vision loss and seizures present) for each of the cognitive tests. The proportion of participants able to recite the alphabet also decreased from Stage 1 to Stage 2 (χ 2 = 12.1, p < 0.01). Cognitive ability declines with advanced disease severity in CLN3 disease, though motor disability in Stage 3 likely contributes to difficulty participating in cognitive assessment at this later disease stage. Understanding the relationship between cognition and CLN3 disease stage may help guide decision making, that is, determining who could or should undergo cognitive assessment for clinical care or for group stratification in disease modifying clinical trials.

papers.title: Benchmarking freely accessible large language models for pediatric epilepsy care: a prospective mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) may support patient education and clinical documentation, but their accuracy, safety, and usability in pediatric epilepsy remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to compare four freely accessible LLMs using standardized pediatric epilepsy scenarios and to evaluate the top-performing model that met the prespecified safety criterion in a supervised clinician workflow assessment.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, two-phase mixed-methods study at the University Hospital at King Abdulaziz University in Jeddah. In phase 1, four freely accessible LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Perplexity) were evaluated using 10 standardized pediatric epilepsy scenarios. Outputs were assessed by pediatric neurologists across factual accuracy, comprehensiveness and relevance, safety, clinical appropriateness, readability and caregiver tailoring, and transparency and sources. Critical safety flags were recorded separately. In phase 2, the model with the highest observed composite score among systems meeting the prespecified safety criterion underwent a supervised clinician workflow assessment using the System Usability Scale (SUS), a caregiver-facing educational-material assessment, and semi-structured interviews.
RESULTS: Forty LLM responses were evaluated. Observed composite scores differed significantly across the four model-specific rater groups (P<0.001); however, because each model was evaluated exclusively by a single rater, the observed differences cannot be attributed to model effects independently of evaluator-specific scoring tendencies. DeepSeek and Gemini generated no critical safety flags, whereas ChatGPT had flags in 3/10 responses (30%) and Perplexity in 8/10 (80%). DeepSeek had the highest observed composite score (4.94/5), compared with 4.42/5 for Gemini, 3.59/5 for ChatGPT, and 2.05/5 for Perplexity, and was therefore selected for phase 2. Clinician approval for caregiver use was higher for responses without safety flags than for flagged responses (82.8% vs. 9.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this specialty-specific benchmark, the evaluated LLMs showed substantial differences in observed accuracy and safety, with DeepSeek achieving the highest observed composite score and no critical safety flags. However, the single-rater-per-model design, small sample, model updates, and limited workflow assessment preclude definitive conclusions about comparative model superiority. These findings support specialty-specific evaluation of LLMs that prioritizes safety and clinical accuracy alongside usability. Larger, independently rated, multi-center studies with repeated model sampling and objective workflow and patient-centered outcomes are needed before routine clinical implementation can be considered.

papers.title: Persistent cerebrospinal fluid tumor cells during transient radiographic response in bilateral retinoblastoma with central nervous system involvement: a pediatric case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central nervous system (CNS) involvement in retinoblastoma carries a poor prognosis, and the frequency and clinical meaning of discordance between structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology are not well defined. This report describes a compartment-specific mixed response and emphasizes the complementary roles of MRI and serial CSF assessment.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 6-year-11-month-old boy presented after 6 months of progressive left proptosis, tearing, and conjunctival injection, without seizures or somnolence. Examination showed marked left proptosis and corneal opacity. MRI demonstrated bilateral ocular abnormalities, direct extension along the left optic nerve and chiasm, and a 29.3 mm × 25.8 mm intracranial lesion; malignant cells were present in CSF. Four cycles of vincristine, carboplatin, and etoposide reduced the intracranial lesion to 8.7 mm × 7.5 mm, but the left intraocular lesion did not clearly regress, optic nerve thickness increased from 4.9 mm after two cycles to 5.4 mm after four cycles, and CSF remained cytologically positive. Treatment was intensified for cycles 5-6 with cyclophosphamide-containing systemic chemotherapy and intrathecal methotrexate plus cytarabine. After six cycles, the intracranial lesion enlarged to 11.4 mm × 8.6 mm, optic nerve thickness increased to 6.7 mm, and CSF tumor cells persisted. Severe myelosuppression, infection, transfusion requirements, and family-related barriers prevented further treatment. The child died in March 2026, approximately 10 months after diagnosis. Germline testing prompted by bilateral disease identified a pathogenic RB1 c.772_776del (p.Asn258GlufsTer11) variant that was absent from parental blood.
CONCLUSIONS: The early reduction in measurable intracranial tumor burden did not represent CSF clearance and was followed by radiographic progression. In selected patients with CNS-involved retinoblastoma, MRI and CSF cytology provide complementary, non-interchangeable information; this single case supports integrated reassessment but does not establish a new response protocol.

papers.title: Mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia in epilepsy (MOGHE)-like spectrum with a unique NRAS c.182A>G (p.Q61R) variant: a case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia in epilepsy (MOGHE) is a recently recognized cortical malformation linked to epilepsy, characterized by subtle cortical and white matter (WM) abnormalities. Typical MOGHE is predominantly associated with somatic SLC35A2 variants, while the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of MOGHE-like cortical malformations remains incompletely understood, with diverse undetermined molecular mechanisms contributing to disease heterogeneity and epileptogenesis.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We report an 8-year-old girl with early-onset, drug-resistant epilepsy localized to the right temporal lobe. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed atypical enlargement and irregular morphological changes of the right temporal lobe with a disrupted gray-white matter (GM-WM) interface, presenting cyst-like malformative changes that deviate from classic MOGHE radiological features. Neuropathological examination demonstrated cortical architectural disturbance, dysoriented neuronal clusters, and mild oligodendroglial hyperplasia consistent with a MOGHE-like spectrum lesion, while no histopathological evidence of low-grade epilepsy-associated tumor or other neoplastic lesions was identified. Whole exome sequencing (WES) identified a heterozygous NRAS c.182A>G (p.Q61R) variant, which is predicted to be functionally deleterious and interpreted as a potentially pathogenic variant based on standard clinical and genetic criteria. The patient achieved favorable post-surgical seizure control, and the pathogenic contribution of this rare NRAS variant requires further validation.
CONCLUSIONS: This case characterizes a rare epileptogenic MOGHE-like cortical malformation driven by a unique NRAS c.182A>G (p.Q61R) variant, expanding the molecular genetic spectrum of MOGHE-spectrum lesions. The findings indicate that alternative RAS-pathway molecular alterations may participate in the development of atypical MOGHE-like malformations and related epileptogenesis. This study underscores the necessity of comprehensive integration of radiological, histopathological, and genetic evidence for accurate diagnosis of atypical cortical developmental lesions, and provides novel insights for future mechanistic exploration and precision therapeutic research in refractory epilepsy associated with cortical malformations.

papers.title: Istradefylline prevents central nervous system oxygen toxicity.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system oxygen toxicity (CNS-OT) is a toxic reaction induced by inhalation of gases with excessively high partial pressure of oxygen, for which effective proactive preventive and therapeutic measures are currently lacking. Building on our previous work implicating adenosine A2A receptor (A2AR) signaling, we examined the prophylactic effects of istradefylline (KW-6002), an approved A2AR antagonist, in male mice. We found that pretreatment oral administration of istradefylline (0.5-20 mg/kg) in mice significantly prolonged the latency to seizure onset and markedly reduced both the intensity and frequency of seizures during a 30-min exposure to 100% oxygen at 5 ATA. Cortical targeted metabolomics showed that HBO exposure decreased GABA and increased glutamate; istradefylline increased cortical GABA without significantly reducing cortical glutamate. Separate ELISA measurements showed lower hippocampal glutamate in istradefylline-treated mice than in HBO-exposed vehicle controls, whereas reductions in the other regions examined were not statistically significant. In the striatum, istradefylline was associated with lower cAMP, immunoreactive PKA protein concentration, and phosphorylated CREB, together with reduced GluA1 Ser845 phosphorylation and increased GABA_A receptor β3 Ser408/409 phosphorylation. In the cortex, malondialdehyde levels decreased and catalase activity increased, whereas glutathione peroxidase activity decreased further. Striatal IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α mRNA levels were also reduced. These findings support a prophylactic effect of istradefylline against HBO-induced seizures in male mice and identify associated changes in neurotransmitter levels, receptor phosphorylation, signaling markers, oxidative-stress measures, and inflammatory-gene expression. These results provide a theoretical basis for the development of proactive preventive and therapeutic strategies for CNS-OT with potential clinical application.

papers.title: Conserved Thalamic Astrocytic Pathology in Mice and Patients Links TBI to Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) can emerge months to years after traumatic brain injury (TBI) and is a major cause of morbidity, yet the pathological processes that distinguish TBI progressing to epilepsy remain poorly defined. Here, we combined longitudinal multimodal imaging, electrophysiology, neuropathology, and human imaging and postmortem analyses to identify cross-species features associated with PTE. In a mouse model of PTE-prone TBI, injury produced widespread brain pathology, whereas animals developing PTE showed disproportionate thalamic atrophy, white-matter abnormalities with reduced optic tract fractional anisotropy, and persistent metabolic alterations. Histological analyses revealed pronounced thalamic astrocytic reactivity, reduced cytoskeletal complexity, and impaired expression of proteins involved in glutamate homeostasis. Using an early ECoG signature to prospectively stratify PTE risk, we found that astrocytic simplification and accumulation of insoluble GFAP were already present during the latent period before spontaneous seizure onset. In patients with PTE, thalamic volume loss and reduced posterior thalamic radiation fractional anisotropy independently improved PTE classification beyond clinical variables. PTE patients also showed reduced pulvinar-centered thalamocortical functional connectivity involving visual and default mode networks. Postmortem tissue further demonstrated pronounced astrocytic reactivity and reduced astrocytic complexity in cortex and thalamus. In contrast, IBA1-defined microglial reactivity did not distinguish PTE from non-PTE at the chronic time points examined. Together, these findings identify a conserved thalamocortical phenotype associated with PTE and show that astrocytic remodeling emerges before spontaneous seizures. The convergence of cellular pathology with structural, metabolic, and functional abnormalities identifies the thalamus as a candidate hub of post-traumatic epileptogenesis and provides translational markers for tracking disease progression after TBI.

papers.title: Transcriptomics-based drug repositioning in a neurocysticercosis rat model identifies putative therapeutic candidates reported to mitigate neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Neurocysticercosis (NCC) is a major cause of epilepsy and neurological symptoms in low- and middle-income countries. Although antiparasitic treatment targets the parasite, it often fails to fully resolve symptoms and can exacerbate brain tissue damage. Using a rat model of NCC and transcriptomic profiling, we assessed the effects of infection and treatment on brain gene expression to uncover disease molecular pathways and identify putative therapeutic candidates through in silico drug repurposing. We analyzed transcriptomic profiles at two stages of infection (4- and 6-month post-infection (MPI)), and after treatment at 6 MPI (6 MPI + T). At 6 MPI, fewer immune-related genes and pathways were enriched compared to 4 MPI, likely due to MAPK pathway repression, but immune activation increased significantly after treatment, possibly due to cyst degeneration. Drug repositioning identified 30 candidate drugs. Among these, vorinostat, ciclosporin, papaverine, valproic acid, and chlorpromazine have been reported to mitigate neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Taken together, these results provide a molecular rationale for drug repositioning in neurocysticercosis; however, further experimental validation in larger cohorts is required to confirm the therapeutic potential of the identified candidates.

papers.title: Altered interictal alpha-band organization in childhood absence epilepsy.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interictal background EEG in childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) may appear normal. We asked whether drug-naive children with CAE differ from controls in alpha frequency and the regional distribution of phase-lagged synchronization, and how these differences depend on participant-specific surrogate baselines and analysis frequency.
METHODS: We analyzed eyes-closed resting EEG (19 channels, 26 s) from 49 drug-naive children with CAE and 83 controls. Individual alpha frequency (IAF) was estimated by spectral parameterization of posterior channels. Weighted phase-lag index (wPLI) at 12 Hz was summarized globally and as the frontal-posterior log-ratio λFP = ln(wPLIF/wPLIP), where F and P denote frontal and posterior within-region means. Participant-specific baselines were obtained from 100 circular-shift surrogates, preserving each channel's wavelet-coefficient sequence up to circular translation while altering inter-channel alignment. Group comparisons used studentized permutation tests. The regional contrast was also evaluated at each participant's IAF.
RESULTS: IAF was lower in patients (8.80 versus 9.42 Hz; p = 0.002). At 12 Hz, controls showed posterior predominance of synchronization (λFP = -0.352), which was largely removed by circular shifting (-0.036), whereas patients' mean regional balance was near zero. After baseline subtraction, the patient-minus-control difference in λFP was 0.332 (95 % CI [0.181, 0.483]; p < 0.001; Hedges' g = 0.79). In the 131 participants with identifiable IAF, the contrast was 0.316 at 12 Hz and 0.124 at IAF (p = 0.139). A direct comparison using within-participant changes supported a larger contrast at 12 Hz (difference 0.192, 95 % CI [0.017, 0.367]; exploratory, unadjusted p = 0.032). The global wPLI difference after baseline subtraction remained uncertain (-0.021, 95 % CI [-0.044, 0.001]; p = 0.069).
CONCLUSIONS: Drug-naive CAE was associated with slower alpha activity and reduced posterior predominance of phase-lagged synchronization at 12 Hz. Circular shifting largely removed the controls' posterior predominance, supporting a difference in regional organization sensitive to inter-channel alignment. The smaller contrast at IAF indicates that analysis frequency materially affects this finding, without establishing that alpha slowing alone explains it.

papers.title: The impact of comorbid headache on surgical outcomes in drug-resistant focal epilepsy.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Headache is a common comorbidity of epilepsy and is closely associated with the poor prognosis of epilepsy. Resection surgery of the epileptogenic focus is an effective treatment method for drug-resistant focal epilepsy (DRFE). However, the relationship between headache and surgical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of comorbid headache and its characteristics on short-term surgical outcomes in DRFE.
METHODS: DRFE patients undergoing resection surgery were consecutively enrolled and followed up for at least one year after surgery. Seizure-free rate within 1 year after surgery was compared between the headache and non-headache groups. Subgroup analysis was performed within the headache group to compare headache characteristics between patients who were seizure-free and those who experienced seizures within 1 year after surgery.
RESULTS: A total of 103 DRFE patients were enrolled, among whom 46 (44.7%) had comorbid headache. Of the 46 patients, 23 experienced unilateral headache, and in 22 of these 23 patients (22/23, 95.7%), the headache side was ipsilateral to the epileptogenic focus. The difference in the seizure-free rate within 1 year after surgery between the headache and non-headache groups was not statistically significant (78.3% vs. 73.7%, p = 0.590). Among DRFE patients with comorbid headache, compared with the seizure within 1 year after surgery group, unilateral headache was significantly more frequent (58.3% vs. 20.0%, p = 0.032), and the mean preoperative visual analogue scale (VAS) score was significantly lower (5.50 ± 2.171 vs. 7.60 ± 1.578, p = 0.007) in the seizure-free within 1 year after surgery group. Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis demonstrated that unilateral headache was independently associated with higher odds of seizure-free within 1 year after surgery (OR = 1.854, 95% CI 1.112-3.092, p = 0.018), whereas the preoperative VAS score was independently associated with lower odds of seizure-free within 1 year after surgery (OR = 0.136, 95% CI 0.020-0.923, p = 0.041).
CONCLUSION: Comorbid headache does not significantly affect short-term surgical outcomes in DRFE patients. However, for DRFE patients with comorbid headache, unilateral headache or a lower preoperative VAS score may serve as potential clinical indicators for favorable short-term surgical outcomes.

papers.title: Cortical physiological arousal following termination of absence seizures.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.abstract: Although the brain state preceding and during absence seizures has been well-characterized, the postictal brain state remains largely unexplored due to the prevailing assumption that absence seizures have minimal or no postictal changes. To address this gap, scalp EEG recordings from 55 patients with 3-4 Hz spike-wave discharges across four multi-site cohorts were analyzed. Spectral power was measured relative to each seizure's preictal baseline, and the postictal period was compared to a time-matched preictal window. Rather than an immediate return to baseline after seizure offset, a significant broadband increase in EEG power was observed in the gamma (>25 Hz) and delta (<4 Hz) frequency bands, followed by a gradual decline over the next 15 s to 30 s. In contrast, no comparable change preceded the seizures. This suggests that recovery from an absence seizure is an active process with a characteristic electrophysiological signature consistent with cortical activation and arousal. Thus, postictal arousal may facilitate exit from the seizure state, and with further work could serve as an electrophysiological marker and therapeutic target for recovery in absence epilepsy.
