papers.title: Repetitive clustered low-voltage fast activity on intracranial electroencephalogram in mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy: A candidate electroencephalographic biomarker study.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE) is a recently recognized cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. It is often magnetic resonance imaging-negative or radiologically resembles focal cortical dysplasias, which makes recognition difficult and limits presurgical counseling. We aimed to identify an intracranial electroencephalographic (iEEG) biomarker that distinguishes MOGHE from other developmental brain lesions encountered in epilepsy surgery.
METHODS: We analyzed long-term stereo-EEG and subdural recordings in a retrospective multicenter test cohort (18 MOGHE, 20 non-MOGHE) to identify an iEEG pattern distinguishing MOGHE from other developmental brain lesions. We then evaluated its diagnostic performance by blinded visual assessment in an independent single-center validation cohort (11 MOGHE, 11 non-MOGHE). Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression tested whether MOGHE histology independently predicted the presence of this pattern after adjustment for spasms, frontal localization, age at seizure onset, and age at implantation. Finally, within MOGHE, we assessed whether resection of the territory exhibiting this pattern was associated with postsurgical seizure freedom.
RESULTS: We identified highly stereotyped clusters of very brief low-voltage fast activity (LVFA), recurring in statuslike episodes lasting several minutes and sometimes lacking clear clinical symptoms. LVFA clusters occurred in 16 of 18 MOGHE and in no non-MOGHE patients in the test cohort. In the validation cohort, visual identification of LVFA clusters correctly classified 10 of 11 MOGHE and 10 of 11 non-MOGHE cases (overall agreement = 90.9%, 95% Wilson confidence interval = 72.2%-97.5%). MOGHE histology was the dominant independent predictor of LVFA clusters. Within MOGHE, resection of LVFA cluster territory was associated with postsurgical seizure freedom (Mann-Whitney U-test, p = .0021).
SIGNIFICANCE: Because LVFA clusters can be recognized visually on routine iEEG without specialized software, they may provide a clinically applicable candidate biomarker for presurgical identification of MOGHE and support surgical planning and outcome prediction. Prospective studies should validate their diagnostic and prognostic utility.

papers.title: Relapsing Anti-NMDAR encephalitis with later detected MOG-IgG-Positive cortical encephalitis: a case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is the most common autoimmune encephalitis. Neuroimaging findings are frequently normal or nonspecific, and predominant cortical involvement at disease onset is uncommon in anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Overlap with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) has been increasingly recognized; therefore, the value of individual reports lies in defining their longitudinal phenotypic evolution and diagnostic limitations.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 28-year-old woman with relapsing anti-NMDAR encephalitis followed for nearly seven years across three episodes (the index attack and two relapses). The initial presentation in 2018 was typical anti-NMDAR encephalitis, with positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) anti-NMDAR antibodies and complete clinical remission after the first episode. The 2022 relapse manifested as focal cortical encephalitis with progressive unilateral cortical swelling, sulcal enhancement, and seizures; MOG-IgG was not tested. In 2025, she developed recurrent headache, intracranial hypertension, and extensive unilateral cortical involvement, with later detected serum MOG-IgG at 1:32. CSF anti-NMDAR and MOG-IgG were not tested at this admission. The episode was therefore adjudicated as MOG-IgG-positive cortical encephalitis within a longitudinal anti-NMDAR/MOGAD overlap course rather than a proven simultaneous dual-antibody relapse. Oral methylprednisolone was followed by clinical and radiological improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Across nearly seven years, this case documents phenotypic evolution from CSF-confirmed anti-NMDAR encephalitis to recurrent unilateral cortical encephalitis and later serum MOG-IgG detection. A changing cortical phenotype should prompt renewed antibody assessment at each recurrence rather than reliance on the index antibody profile. Because MOG-IgG was not tested in earlier episodes and CSF anti-NMDAR was not tested in 2025, the timing and mechanistic contribution of each antibody cannot be determined.

papers.title: Multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks in older adults with diabetes: A national population-based network analysis.
papers.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
papers.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to characterize multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks among older adults with diabetes in China.
MATERIALS: This cross-sectional study analysed data from older adults aged ≥65 years with diabetes from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Network and hierarchical clustering analyses were used to examine co-occurrence patterns among 17 chronic physical and mental conditions.
RESULTS: A total of 1408 participants with diabetes were included, comprising 593 male participants (42.1%) and 815 female participants (57.9%). Overall, 91.6% of participants had ≥1 additional chronic condition, and 71.3% had ≥2 additional chronic conditions. Hypertension (75.5%), heart disease (36.7%) and affective disorder (33.7%) were the three most common conditions; the hypertension-heart disease combination was the leading comorbidity pair (31.75%). Arthritis ranked highest for strength, closeness and betweenness in the overall network; epilepsy also ranked highly for strength and betweenness, particularly among participants aged ≥75 years and in the central and western regions. Five comorbidity clusters emerged from hierarchical clustering, with centrality profiles differing by age, sex and region.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicated that multimorbidity burden was high among people with diabetes aged ≥65 years in China and was characterized by distinct network structures and clustering patterns. Arthritis and epilepsy showed high centrality in the comorbidity network, and network characteristics differed across age, sex and regional groups. These findings suggest that health management for older adults with diabetes should address not only common cardiometabolic conditions but also musculoskeletal, neurological and mental health problems.

papers.title: Expanding mutational landscape and clinical phenotype of the CASK-related neurological disorders.
papers.abstract: CASK-related disorders comprise two main phenotypes: severe microcephaly with pontocerebellar hypoplasia (MICPCH), typically caused by truncating variants, and milder X-linked intellectual disability (XLID), usually associated with missense variants. We aimed to characterize this molecular spectrum within an underrepresented national cohort. We evaluated 18 affected individuals from 16 unrelated families with CASK variants identified through exome or genome sequencing. Clinical, neurodevelopmental and neuroimaging findings were systematically reviewed. Selected missense variants were evaluated by in silico prediction tools and structural modeling. We identified 16 distinct CASK variants, 11 of which are novel, including frameshift, stop-gain, splice-site, and missense variants, as well as one large deletion. Consistent with known genotype-phenotype correlations, null alleles resulted in the severe MICPCH phenotype, while presumed hypomorphic alleles were associated with XLID. However, unlike previous reports, our MICPCH patients exhibited a higher frequency of dysmorphic facial features (86%), skeletal anomalies (57%) and sensorineural hearing loss (43%). Furthermore, contrary to the literature suggesting a milder epilepsy in females due to X-inactivation, 63% of our female patients with MICPCH presented with recurrent seizures. This cohort broadens both the molecular and phenotypic spectrum of CASK-related disorders. Findings reinforce that truncating variants predominantly cause MICPCH, while missense variants can lead to various outcomes depending on domain-level structural impact. We demonstrate that the CASK phenotypic spectrum is broader than previously recognized, frequently involving distinctive facial dysmorphism, skeletal defects and hearing impairment, suggesting that CASK plays a critical role not only in synaptic function but also in wider developmental processes.

papers.title: Molecular Diagnosis in Children With Febrile Seizures: Beyond the Conventional Clinical Classification.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Febrile seizures (FS) are currently classified as simple or complex primarily to describe seizure characteristics, with limited ability to identify the underlying etiology. We evaluated whether molecular diagnosis could complement conventional classification and improve the diagnosis and management of FS.
METHODS: This nationwide, multi-center, prospective cohort study, conducted from January 2019 to February 2023, enrolled patients who were clinically diagnosed with FS. The panel targeted 189 genes associated with fever-induced seizures. Initially, children were categorized into simple febrile seizures (SFS) and complex febrile seizures (CFS) groups based on medical history and clinical evaluation. Variant classification followed the ACMG guidelines. We analyzed the cohort demographic characteristics, potential genetic etiologies across different clinical phenotypes, and clinical utility of genetic diagnosis.
RESULTS: Our study included 3300 children with FS, and ultimately analyzed sequencing data from 2552 children, of whom 273 received a positive diagnosis. The molecular diagnostic yield was 11% (273 out of 2552 patients), with the top 10 genes accounting for 70.4% of all confirmed genetic diagnoses. No significant difference in molecular diagnostic yield was observed between the SFS (9.5%, 111/1163) and CFS (11.7%, 162/1389) groups (p = 0.085). Molecular diagnostics had immediate clinical utility, influencing management (76.2%) and informing prognosis (72.6%). The cost of a single panel sequencing for a three-person family was $240, with a turnaround time of 14 days.
INTERPRETATION: Molecular diagnosis may improve the diagnosis of FS by identifying genetic fever-sensitive epilepsies that may be missed by phenotype-based classification, with implications for risk stratification and individualized management.
